relevance_reason: The paper does not report germline variants causing rheumatoid arthritis, but provides functional and immunological evidence in mice and RA patients identifying RPL23A as an autoantigen targeted by T cells and autoantibodies in RA, relevant to pathogenesis of the disorder.

findings.statement: Ito et al. (2014) used BALB/c SKG mice, which develop T cell-mediated spontaneous autoimmune arthritis resembling RA due to a hypomorphic point mutation of ZAP-70, to isolate arthritogenic T cell receptors; among nine retrogenic strains each expressing a distinct TCR cloned from GFP- Valpha2+ Vbeta6+ CD4+ T cells of arthritic joints, those expressing the 7-39 or 6-39 TCR spontaneously developed arthritis at incidences of 80.0% and 27.3%, respectively, with mononuclear cell infiltration, pannus formation and cartilage destruction.
quotes: For example, a hypomorphic point mutation of ζ-associated protein 70 (ZAP-70), a TCR-proximal signaling molecule, causes T cell-mediated spontaneous autoimmune arthritis in mice, which resembles RA.

Among nine retrogenic strains each expressing a distinct TCR, the ones expressing 7–39 or 6–39 TCR spontaneously developed arthritis at the incidence of 80.0% and 27.3%, respectively (Fig. 1A–C and fig. S4A–C).
Arthritic joints in retrogenic 7–39 (R7–39) mice showed mononuclear cell infiltration, pannus formation and cartilage destruction (Fig. 1D).

findings.statement: Ito et al. (2014) reported that 66.7% of R7-39 retrogenic mice also developed chronic dermatitis exhibiting hyperkeratosis and parakeratosis, histopathological features of human psoriasis, whereas R6-39 mice did not; 7-39 TCR-transduced cells differentiated into monoclonal activated/memory CD4+ T cells that transferred both arthritis and dermatitis into other Rag2-/- mice, and the same TCR gene transferred into ZAP-70-intact BALB/c bone marrow did not cause arthritis because the T cells were largely negatively selected in the thymus or remained naive and anergic.
quotes: Some (66.7%) of R7–39, but not R6–39, mice also developed chronic dermatitis, which exhibited hyperkeratosis and parakeratosis, histopathological features of human psoriasis (Fig. 1E–F and fig. S5).

In contrast to 7–39 TCR gene-transfected Rag2−/− BM cells with the SKG ZAP-70 mutation, 7–39 TCR gene-transfected ZAP-70-intact Rag2−/− BALB/c BM cells did not cause arthritis in retrogenic mice (designated W7–39 mice).

In W7–39 mice, the majority of 7–39 TCR-expressing CD4+ T cells were negatively selected in the thymus, and those which had escaped thymic negative selection, exhibited a naïve non-activated phenotype, indicating their dormant or anergic state

phenotypes.text: chronic dermatitis with hyperkeratosis and parakeratosis

findings.statement: Ito et al. (2014) identified by immunoblotting with sera from B cell-reconstituted R7-39 mice and mass spectrometry that the self-antigen recognized by the arthritogenic 7-39 TCR was the ubiquitously expressed 18-kD 60S ribosomal protein L23a (RPL23A), whose amino acid sequence is 100% conserved between mice and humans; recombinant RPL23A stimulated 7-39 hybridoma cells in a dose-dependent, MHC class II I-Ad-dependent manner, with the RPL23A71-90 peptide being the most potent stimulatory epitope.
quotes: The sera from these ‘B cell-reconstituted’ mice specifically reacted with a protein of 18 kD from the cell extract of P3U1 cells (Fig. 2A). Mass spectrometric analysis identified this protein as RPL23A, a component of the 60S subunit of ribosome (fig. S11).
The amino acid sequence of RPL23A is 100% conserved between mice and humans.

In addition, recombinant RPL23A protein specifically stimulated the 7–39 hybridoma cells in a dose dependent, class II major histocompatibility complex (MHC) I-Ad dependent manner (Fig. 2D and fig. S12). Among 20mer RPL23A peptides with consecutive overlapping of 5 amino acid residues, RPL23A71–90 peptide stimulated 7–39 TCR most potently

findings.statement: Ito et al. (2014) showed that CD4+ T cells, but not sera, from B cell-reconstituted R7-39 mice induced arthritis upon transfer into Rag2-/- mice, and that CD4+ T cells from arthritic joints or regional lymph nodes produced IL-17A, IFN-gamma and GM-CSF upon stimulation with RPL23A protein or the RPL23A71-90 peptide; regulatory T cells from BALB/c or SKG mice failed to suppress arthritis induced by activated or memory R7-39 TCR+ CD4+ T cells, although they effectively suppressed naive arthritogenic T cells.
quotes: Upon transfer, CD4+ T cells, but not sera, from B cell-reconstituted R7–39 mice induced arthritis in Rag2−/− mice (fig. S15). Indeed, CD4+ T cells from arthritic joints or the regional lymph nodes of R7–39 mice produced inflammatory cytokines including IL-17A and interferon (IFN)-γ, and granulocyte macrophage-colony stimulating factor (GM-CSF)

Treg cells from either ZAP-70-intact BALB/c or ZAP-70-mutant SKG mice failed to suppress arthritis development in Rag2−/− mice when co-transferred with phenotypically activated or memory R7–39 TCR+ CD4+ T cells (fig. S7 and S18), albeit Treg cells were capable of suppressing naïve arthritogenic T cells effectively.

findings.statement: Ito et al. (2014) found by ELISA that serum anti-RPL23A IgG autoantibodies were present in a significantly higher proportion of rheumatoid arthritis patients (16.8% of 374) than in healthy controls (1.3% of 74); 2 of 23 psoriatic arthritis patients (8.7%) were positive, whereas none of 11 osteoarthritis, 30 systemic lupus erythematosus, or 10 polymyositis/dermatomyositis patients were positive.
quotes: A significantly higher proportion of RA patients (16.8%, n=374) were positive for serum anti-RPL23A IgG-type autoantibodies compared with healthy controls (1.3%, n=74)) (Fig. 4C).

Two out of 23 psoriatic arthritis (PsA) patients (8.7%) but none of OA (n=11), systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) (n=30), or polymyositis/dermatomyositis (PM/DM) (n=10) patients were positive for the autoantibody.

findings.statement: Ito et al. (2014) detected, in the synovial fluid of a subset of RA patients, CD4+ T cells that produced IFN-gamma upon stimulation with recombinant RPL23A (24 RA patients versus 9 healthy individuals tested), and demonstrated that RPL23A mRNA was ubiquitously expressed in healthy human tissues and that RPL23A protein was present in the cytoplasm of synovial cells, including CD55+ fibroblast-like synoviocytes, in both RA and osteoarthritis synovium; the authors suggested these responses may play a pathogenic role at least in a subset of patients with RA or psoriatic arthritis.
quotes: In addition, in synovial fluid of a subset of RA patients, we detected CD4+ T cells producing IFN-γ upon stimulation with RPL23A (Fig. 4D–E).
In synovial tissues of RA and also apparently normal synovial tissues of osteoarthritis (OA), RPL23A was detected in the cytoplasm of synovial cells, including CD55+ FLSs (Fig. 4B).

These findings in humans, together with the key role of anti-RPL23A T-cell responses for autoimmune arthritis and psoriasis-like dermatitis in mice, suggest that the responses may play a pathogenic role at least in a subset of patients with RA or PsA.

phenotypes.text: RPL23A-reactive IFN-gamma-producing CD4+ T cells in synovial fluid

findings.statement: Ito et al. (2014) noted that B cell-reconstituted R7-39 mice and arthritic SKG mice developed antibodies reacting with cyclic citrullinated peptides as observed in RA patients, but found no significant difference in anti-RPL23A antibody titer whether assessed with citrullinated or non-citrullinated RPL23A protein, and the stimulatory RPL23A71-90 peptide contained no arginine residue convertible to citrulline.
quotes: B cell-reconstituted R7–39 mice and arthritic SKG mice developed antibodies reacting with cyclic citrullinated peptides (CCP) as observed in RA patients (fig. S14A); yet, there was no significant difference in anti-RPL23A antibody titer whether it was assessed with citrullinated or non-citrullinated RPL23A protein (fig. S14B–C). In addition, the RPL23A71–90 peptide recognized by 7–39 TCR contained no arginine residue to be converted to citrulline (table S3).

findings.statement: Ito et al. (2014) proposed that, since genetic polymorphism in a T cell signaling molecule is a major determinant of genetic susceptibility to human autoimmune diseases including RA, such genetic variation might at least in part alter thymic selection and thereby form a TCR repertoire capable of causing autoimmune disease.
quotes: In addition, given that genetic polymorphism in a signaling molecule in T cells is a major determinant of genetic susceptibility to various human autoimmune diseases including RA, such a genetic variation might, at least in part, alter thymic selection, hence forming a TCR repertoire for causing autoimmune disease.

relevance_reason: An eQTL study in healthy people's immune cells. It found that rheumatoid arthritis susceptibility alleles are enriched for T cell-specific cis-regulatory effects, which points to a pathogenic cell type.

findings.statement: Raj et al. (2014) did an expression quantitative trait locus (eQTL) study of purified naive CD4+ T cells and CD14+CD16- monocytes from 461 healthy individuals of European, African American, and East Asian ancestry. They found that susceptibility alleles for rheumatoid arthritis, as well as for multiple sclerosis and type 1 diabetes, were enriched for T cell-specific cis-regulatory effects. Susceptibility alleles for Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease were instead enriched for monocyte-specific effects. The authors concluded that this polarization implicates specific immune cell types in these diseases.
quotes: variants associated with some diseases display a preponderance of T cell–specific cis-regulatory effects: These include susceptibility alleles for multiple sclerosis, rheumatoid arthritis, and type 1 diabetes
Multiple sclerosis and rheumatoid arthritis are enriched in T cell effects (green), whereas Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s diseases are enriched in monocyte effects (orange).
We note an over-representation of T cell-specific eQTLs among susceptibility alleles for autoimmune diseases and of monocyte-specific eQTLs among Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease variants.
findings.population: European American, African American, East Asian American (Boston, Massachusetts)

findings.statement: Raj et al. (2014) found that, of 425 GWAS SNPs associated with one or more autoimmune diseases, 143 had cis-regulatory effects on 164 genes in monocytes and/or T cells. This was a significant enrichment (permutation P < 1 x 10(-4)).
quotes: Of the 425 GWAS SNPs associated with one or more autoimmune disease, 143 have cis-regulatory effects on 164 genes in monocytes and/or T cells

relevance_reason: Large trans-ethnic GWAS meta-analysis that identified 42 new rheumatoid arthritis risk loci, bringing the total to 101, and examined biological and drug-target links for RA.

findings.statement: Okada et al. (2014) performed a three-stage trans-ethnic genome-wide association meta-analysis of rheumatoid arthritis in 29,880 cases and 73,758 controls of European and Asian ancestry, evaluating about 10 million SNPs. They identified 42 novel RA risk loci at genome-wide significance (P < 5.0 x 10(-8)), bringing the total number of RA risk loci to 101, including the MHC region.
quotes: Here we performed a genome-wide association study meta-analysis in a total of >100,000 subjects of European and Asian ancestries (29,880 RA cases and 73,758 controls), by evaluating ∼10 million single-nucleotide polymorphisms.

In a combined analysis of Stages I–III, we identified 42 novel loci with P < 5.0×10−8 in either of the trans-ethnic, European, or Asian meta-analyses. This increases the total number of RA risk loci to 101

findings.statement: In Stage I, Okada et al. (2014) combined 22 GWAS of 19,234 cases and 61,565 controls and identified 57 loci at genome-wide significance, 17 of them novel. Loci with P < 5.0 x 10(-6) were then tested in Stage II (in silico) and Stage III (de novo) replication studies totaling 10,646 cases and 12,193 controls.
quotes: In Stage I, we combined 22 GWAS for 19,234 cases and 61,565 controls of European and Asian ancestry–.
Stage I meta-analysis identified 57 loci that satisfied a genome-wide significance threshold of P < 5.0×10−8, including 17 novel loci
We then conducted a two-step replication study (Stage II for in-silico and Stage III for de-novo) in 10,646 RA cases and 12,193 controls for the loci with P < 5.0×10−6 in Stage I.

findings.statement: The novel RA loci reported by Okada et al. (2014) included SNPs near TNFRSF9, IRF4, CDK6, ETS1, CD226, SYNGR1 (rs909685; trans-ethnic OR 1.13, P = 1.4 x 10(-16)), ATM, ILF3, IL20RB, and P2RY10 on the X chromosome.

Across the 101 loci, Okada et al. (2014) found that risk allele frequencies and odds ratios were significantly correlated between Europeans and Asians, although 5 loci showed population-specific associations. The 100 non-MHC loci explained 5.5% of heritability in Europeans and 4.7% in Asians. The authors concluded that genetic risk of RA is largely shared between the two populations.
quotes: Comparison of 101 RA risk loci revealed significant correlations of risk allele frequencies (RAF) and odds ratios (OR) between Europeans and Asians (Extended Data Fig. 3a–c; Spearman’s ρ = 0.67 for RAF and 0.76 for OR; P < 1.0×10−13), although 5 loci demonstrated population-specific associations

the 100 RA risk loci outside of the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) region explained 5.5% and 4.7% of heritability in Europeans and Asians, respectively, with 1.6% of the heritability by the novel loci.
These observations support our hypothesis that the genetic risk of RA is shared, in general, among Asians and Europeans

findings.statement: Of 34 cell types tested, Okada et al. (2014) found that RA risk alleles were significantly enriched in H3K4me3 histone peaks only in primary CD4+ regulatory T cells. Pathway analysis showed enrichment for T-cell pathways, as well as B-cell and cytokine signaling pathways (IL-10, interferon, GM-CSF).
quotes: Of 34 cell types investigated, we observed significant enrichment of RA risk alleles with trimethylation of histone H3 at lysine 4 (H3K4me3) peaks in primary CD4+ regulatory T cells (Treg cells; P < 1.0×10−5).

We observed enrichment (FDR-q < 0.05) for T cell related pathways, consistent with cell-specific epigenetic marks, as well as enrichment for B cell and cytokine signaling pathways (e.g., IL-10, interferon, GM-CSF).

findings.statement: Genes at RA risk loci overlapped significantly with genes for primary immunodeficiency (14 of 194; strongest in the immune dysregulation category, with no overlap in innate immunity). They also overlapped with genes somatically mutated in hematologic cancers but not other cancers, and with knockout-mouse hematopoietic, immune, and cellular phenotypes. Okada et al. (2014) reported that about two-thirds of RA loci were shared with other traits, including vitiligo and primary biliary cirrhosis.
quotes: we evaluated whether genes from RA risk loci overlapped with PID genes, and observed significant overlap (14/194 = 7.2%, P = 1.2×10−4; Fig. 1a and Extended Data Fig. 5c).
we observed significant overlap with hematological cancers (17/251 = 6.8%, P = 1.2×10−4; Fig. 1b and Extended Data Fig. 5d), but not from non-hematological cancers (6/221 = 2.7%, P = 0.56).

We found that approximately two-thirds of RA risk loci demonstrated pleiotropy with other human phenotypes (Extended Data Fig. 4), including immune-related diseases (e.g., vitiligo, primary biliary cirrhosis)

findings.statement: Okada et al. (2014) scored the 377 genes at the 100 non-MHC loci against 8 criteria, including missense variants, cis-eQTL effects, protein-protein interactions, and mouse knockout phenotypes. They defined 98 genes as candidate biological RA risk genes, such as IL3 and CSF2 at 5q31. RA risk SNPs at 44 loci showed cis-eQTL effects, and 16% of risk SNPs were in linkage disequilibrium with missense SNPs.
quotes: Ninety-eight genes (26.0%) had a score ≥2, which we defined as “candidate biological RA risk genes”. Nineteen loci included multiple biological RA risk genes (e.g., IL3 and CSF2 at 5q31), while no biological gene was selected from 40 loci
we found that RA risk SNPs in 44 loci showed cis-eQTL effects (FDR-q or permutation P < 0.05; Extended Data Table 2).
Sixteen percent of SNPs were in LD with missense SNPs (r2 > 0.80; Extended Data Fig. 5a–b).

findings.statement: Targets of approved RA drugs were significantly enriched, 3.7-fold, among the 98 biological RA risk genes and their protein-interaction partners. These targets included those of tocilizumab (IL6R), tofacitinib (JAK3), and abatacept (CTLA4-Ig). Okada et al. (2014) suggested that the cancer-drug targets CDK6 and CDK4 could be candidates for drug repurposing, noting that flavopiridol improves disease in animal models of RA.
quotes: Twenty-seven drug target genes of approved RA drugs demonstrated significant overlap with 98 biological RA risk genes and 2,332 genes from the expanded PPI network (18 genes overlapped; 3.7-fold enrichment by permutation analysis, P < 1.0×10−5; Fig. 3b).
Examples of approved RA therapies identified by this analysis include tocilizumab, (anti-IL6R), tofacitinib (JAK3 inhibitor), and abatacept (CTLA4-Ig; Fig. 3c and Extended Data Fig. 8).

We highlight CDK6 and CDK4, targets of three approved drugs for different types of cancer (Fig. 3d). In support for repurposing, one CDK6/CDK4 inhibitor, flavopiridol, has been shown to ameliorate disease activity in animal models of RA.

relevance_reason: Case-control copy number association study showing FCGR3B deletion is linked to RA susceptibility, especially rheumatoid factor-positive disease.

findings.statement: Robinson et al. (2012) used a novel quantitative sequence variant assay together with an adapted paralogue ratio test to study copy number variants (CNVs) of FCGR3A and FCGR3B in 1,115 RA patients and 654 healthy volunteers. They analyzed the data with CNVtools, which accounts for batch effects and for uncertainty in copy number assignment. FCGR3B deletions were overrepresented in RA (OR 1.50, P = 0.028), and the association was stronger in rheumatoid factor-positive disease (OR 1.61, P = 0.011).
quotes: examine independent CNVs carrying FCGR3A and FCGR3B in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) compared with healthy volunteers (n = 1,115 and 654, respectively)

in line with previous studies, there was evidence of overrepresentation of FCGR3B deletions in RA (odds ratio [OR] 1.50, P = 0.028), which was more apparent in rheumatoid factor positive disease (OR 1.61, P = 0.011)

findings.statement: Robinson et al. (2012) found no association between RA and either duplications or deletions of FCGR3A.
quotes: Evidence for association with neither duplications nor deletions of FCGR3A was found

findings.statement: Robinson et al. (2012) showed that FcγRIIIb expression on neutrophils correlated with FCGR3B gene copy number. They suggested that neutrophils may play an important role in RA pathogenesis, possibly through reduced FcγRIIIb-mediated clearance of immune complexes.
quotes: The level of FcγRIIIb, encoded by FCGR3B, expression on neutrophils was shown to correlate with gene copy number.
our results may highlight an important role for neutrophils in the pathogenesis of RA, potentially through reduced FcγRIIIb-mediated immune complex clearance

relevance_reason: Genetic association study of known RA risk alleles in a multi-ethnic cohort built from electronic health records, stratified by ACPA status; adds evidence on how RA genetic risk is shared across ancestries and serologic subsets.

findings.statement: Kurreeman et al. (2011) used electronic health record (EHR) data linked to biospecimens to assemble a multi-ethnic case-control cohort of 1,515 rheumatoid arthritis cases and 1,480 controls, matched for genetic ancestry and anti-citrullinated protein antibody (ACPA) status. In individuals of European ancestry, the odds ratios and aggregate genetic risk score (GRS) of known RA risk alleles were nearly identical to those from a GWAS of 5,539 autoantibody-positive RA cases and 20,169 controls.
quotes: In 1,515 EHR-derived RA cases and 1,480 controls matched for both genetic ancestry and disease-specific autoantibodies (anti-citrullinated protein antibodies [ACPA]), we demonstrate that the odds ratios and aggregate genetic risk score (GRS) of known RA risk alleles measured in individuals of European ancestry within our EHR cohort are nearly identical to those derived from a genome-wide association study (GWAS) of 5,539 autoantibody-positive RA cases and 20,169 controls.

findings.statement: Kurreeman et al. (2011) applied the same approach to other ethnic groups and found a large overlap in the genetic risk score for rheumatoid arthritis among individuals of European, African, East Asian, and Hispanic ancestry. They concluded that the genetic basis of RA risk is similar among cases of diverse ancestry.
quotes: We extend this approach to other ethnic groups and identify a large overlap in the GRS among individuals of European, African, East Asian, and Hispanic ancestry.
Our study demonstrates that the genetic basis of rheumatoid arthritis risk is similar among cases of diverse ancestry divided into subsets based on ACPA status

findings.statement: Kurreeman et al. (2011) found that the distribution of a genetic risk score based on 28 non-HLA rheumatoid arthritis risk alleles in ACPA-positive cases partially overlapped with that in the ACPA-negative subgroup of RA cases.
quotes: We also demonstrate that the distribution of a GRS based on 28 non-HLA risk alleles in ACPA+ cases partially overlaps with ACPA- subgroup of RA cases.

relevance_reason: A large GWAS meta-analysis with replication that identified 7 new susceptibility loci for autoantibody-positive rheumatoid arthritis, refined known loci, and listed suggestive loci.

findings.statement: Stahl et al. (2010) performed a GWAS meta-analysis of 5,539 autoantibody-positive RA cases and 20,169 controls of European descent. They replicated the results in an independent set of 6,768 cases and 8,806 controls. Of 34 SNPs selected for replication, 10 reached genome-wide significance (P < 5 x 10(-8)) in the combined analysis of 41,282 samples. Seven of these were new RA risk loci, near genes including IL6ST, SPRED2, RBPJ, CCR6, IRF5, and PXK. With these loci, the number of confirmed RA risk loci in individuals of European ancestry rose to 31.
quotes: we conducted a genome-wide association study meta-analysis of 5,539 autoantibody-positive individuals with rheumatoid arthritis (cases) and 20,169 controls of European descent, followed by replication in an independent set of 6,768 rheumatoid arthritis cases and 8,806 controls
Of 34 SNPs selected for replication, 7 new rheumatoid arthritis risk alleles were identified at genome-wide significance (P < 5 x 10(-8)) in an analysis of all 41,282 samples.
These new associations bring the total number of confirmed rheumatoid arthritis risk loci to 31 among individuals of European ancestry.

findings.statement: Stahl et al. (2010) identified 3 RA risk loci that had not previously been implicated in RA or in any other autoimmune disease. The first was rs934734 at 2p14 (P overall = 5.3 x 10(-10)), within intron 1 of SPRED2. The second was rs6859219 at 5q11 (P overall = 9.6 x 10(-12)), in ANKRD55; the immunologic candidate IL6ST lies about 150 kb away, outside the region of LD. The third was rs26232 at 5q21 (P overall = 4.1 x 10(-8)), in an intron of the predicted gene C5orf30, where there was no obvious biologic candidate gene. Replication odds ratios for the minor alleles were 1.13, 0.85, and 0.93, respectively.
quotes: The SNPs are located at chromosome 2p14 (rs934734, Poverall=5.3×10−10), 5q11 (rs6859219, Poverall=9.6×10−12) and 5q21 (rs26232, Poverall=4.1×10−8). Replication sample odds ratios (for minor alleles) were 1.13, 0.85 and 0.93, respectively (Table 3).

At 5q11, the most significant SNP (rs6859219) is located in ANKRD55, an ankyrin repeat domain-containing gene of unknown function (Figure 1B). A more compelling immunological candidate, interleukin 6 signal transducer (IL6ST), lies ~150 kilobases (kb) proximal but outside the region of LD with associated SNPs.
At 5q21, there is no obvious biological candidate gene; SNP rs26232 lies within the intron of predicted gene C5orf30 (Figure 1C).

findings.statement: Stahl et al. (2010) found that 3 SNPs at loci previously implicated in other autoimmune diseases were also associated with RA. The 3p14 SNP rs13315591 near PXK (P overall = 4.6 x 10(-8)) lies 187 kb from an SNP associated with SLE. The 4p15 SNP rs874040 near RBPJ (P overall = 1.0 x 10(-16)) is in complete LD with a type 1 diabetes SNP, and the same allele confers risk in both diseases. The 6q27 SNP rs3093023 in CCR6 (P overall = 1.5 x 10(-11)) is in LD with an SNP associated with Crohn disease.
quotes: These 3 SNPs are located at chromosome 3p14 (rs13315591, near PXK, Poverall=4.6×10−8), 4p15 (rs874040, near RBPJ, Poverall=1.0×10−16) and 6q27 (rs3093023, in CCR6, Poverall=1.5×10−11).
The 4p15/RBPJ SNP is in complete LD (r2 = 1) with a SNP associated with risk of type 1 diabetes (T1D, rs10517086), and the same allele confers risk in both diseases.

findings.statement: Stahl et al. (2010) found that the IRF5 SNP rs10488631, selected because of its association with SLE, was convincingly associated with autoantibody-positive RA (P replication = 1.2 x 10(-6); P overall = 4.2 x 10(-11)). There was also an association with the group 3 SNP rs4728142 (P GWAS = 7.2 x 10(-6)), which is in LD with a variant that alters IRF5 polyadenylation and expression. There was no association with the group 2 SNP rs729302. Conditional analyses indicated that the group 1 and group 3 effects were independent.
quotes: The IRF5 SNP rs10488631 (PGWAS =2.8×10−6), chosen because of its association in SLE, was convincingly associated with autoantibody positive RA in our study (Preplication=1.2×10−6, Poverall=4.2×10−11).

In addition to the group 1 SNP, rs10488631, we found evidence for association with group 3 SNP rs4728142 (PGWAS=7.2×10−6), which is in LD with a variant that alters IRF5 polyadenylation and expression.
Conditional analyses indicated that the group 1 and group 3 effects are independent (Supplementary Table 3 online).

findings.statement: At the known CCL21 locus, Stahl et al. (2010) identified a new SNP, rs951005 (P overall = 3.9 x 10(-10)), that had little LD with the previously associated SNP rs2812378. The association of rs951005 remained significant after conditioning on rs2812378, indicating partly independent effects.
quotes: Our new CCL21 SNP has little LD with the previous RA risk-associated SNP rs2812378 (PGWAS=1.6×10−7; r2=0.06 and D’=0.83).
the new SNP rs951005 remains significant (P = 1.7×10−5) conditional on the previously known SNP rs2812378; conditional on rs951005, rs2812378 remains nominally significant (P = 0.01).

findings.statement: At the IL2RA locus, Stahl et al. (2010) found that the SNP rs706778 was associated with RA (P overall = 3.3 x 10(-11)). This SNP correlated strongly with the type 1 diabetes risk haplotype tagged by rs2104286(T)-rs11594656(T). Conditional and haplotype analyses showed that this haplotype explained RA risk better than rs706778 did.
quotes: In our GWAS dataset, rs706778 correlated strongly with the T1D risk haplotype (r2=0.83), and conditional and haplotype analyses demonstrated that risk of RA is better explained by this haplotype [rs2104286(T)-rs11594656(T)] than by rs706778

findings.statement: Stahl et al. (2010) provided definitive evidence that the AFF3 locus is associated with autoantibody-positive RA (rs11676922; P overall = 1.0 x 10(-14); OR = 1.14).
quotes: Our study provides definitive evidence that this locus is associated with risk of autoantibody positive RA (rs11676922, Poverall=1.0×10−14, OR=1.14).

findings.statement: Stahl et al. (2010) reported 11 more SNPs that replicated at P < 0.05 without reaching genome-wide significance. These included SNPs near IL6R, CD247, IL2/IL21, ZEB1, SH2B3, BATF, CD19/NFATC2IP, IKZF3, UBASH3A, and UBE2L3, many of them validated autoimmune risk alleles. Of 18 tested SNPs in LD with validated autoimmune risk alleles, 5 reached genome-wide significance and 7 showed suggestive association. The authors concluded that these results underscored the overlap between the genetic bases of RA and other autoimmune diseases.
quotes: An additional 11 SNPs replicated at P < 0.05, many of which are validated autoimmune risk alleles, suggesting that most represent genuine rheumatoid arthritis risk alleles.
Of these, 5 demonstrated genome-wide (Poverall<5×10−8) and 7 showed suggestive (Preplication<0.05) evidence of association in our study; only 6 showed no evidence of association in replication.

findings.statement: Stahl et al. (2010) noted that several of the associations, including those at RBPJ, CCR6, and CD247, further implicate T cells in RA pathogenesis. They also suggested that CCR6 could be a therapeutic target, because anti-CCR6 antibodies inhibit arthritis in mice.
quotes: Several of the SNP associations further implicate T-cells in RA pathogenesis.
Intriguingly, anti-CCR6 monoclonal antibodies substantially inhibit mouse arthritis, suggesting that CCR6 could be a therapeutic target in RA.

findings.statement: Stahl et al. (2010) estimated that the more than 30 validated non-MHC RA risk alleles explain 3.9% of total disease variance, of which 0.67% is due to the new alleles. Known genetic factors overall, including an estimated 12% for the MHC, explain only 16% of disease variance. In contrast, more than half the risk of autoantibody-positive RA is thought to be genetic.
quotes: We estimate that the now >30 validated non-MHC RA risk alleles explain 3.9% of the total disease variance, with 0.67% due to the new RA risk alleles reported here.
genetic discoveries explain only 16% of disease variance (including an estimated 12% for the MHC), whereas more than half the risk of autoantibody positive RA is thought to be genetic.

relevance_reason: GWAS identifying CCR6 as a rheumatoid arthritis susceptibility locus with functional regulatory variant data.

findings.statement: Through a genome-wide association study of rheumatoid arthritis in Japanese individuals, Kochi et al. (2010) identified a polymorphism in CCR6 at 6q27, rs3093024, that was associated with RA susceptibility and was validated in 2 independent Japanese replication cohorts (a total of 7,069 cases and 20,727 controls; overall odds ratio = 1.19, P = 7.7 x 10(-19)).
quotes: we identified a polymorphism in CCR6, the gene encoding chemokine (C-C motif) receptor 6 (a surface marker for Th17 cells) at 6q27, that was associated with rheumatoid arthritis susceptibility

validated in two independent replication cohorts from Japan (rs3093024, a total of 7,069 individuals with rheumatoid arthritis (cases) and 20,727 controls, overall odds ratio = 1.19, P = 7.7 x 10(-19))

findings.statement: Kochi et al. (2010) identified a triallelic dinucleotide polymorphism of CCR6 (CCR6DNP) in strong linkage disequilibrium with rs3093024 that showed effects on gene transcription. The CCR6DNP genotype correlated with CCR6 expression level and was associated with the presence of IL-17 in the sera of RA patients; the authors suggested that CCR6 is critically involved in IL-17-driven autoimmunity.
quotes: We identified a triallelic dinucleotide polymorphism of CCR6 (CCR6DNP) in strong linkage disequilibrium with rs3093024 that showed effects on gene transcription.
The CCR6DNP genotype was correlated with the expression level of CCR6 and was associated with the presence of interleukin-17 (IL-17) in the sera of subjects with rheumatoid arthritis.
These results suggest that CCR6 is critically involved in IL-17-driven autoimmunity in human diseases.

findings.statement: Kochi et al. (2010) found that CCR6DNP was also associated with susceptibility to Graves disease and Crohn disease.
quotes: Moreover, CCR6DNP was associated with susceptibility to Graves' and Crohn's diseases.

relevance_reason: This genome-wide CNV association study included about 2,000 UK rheumatoid arthritis cases. It found that CNVs in the HLA region are associated with RA, and it did not replicate the reported CCL3L1 CNV association.

findings.statement: In a genome-wide association study of 3,432 polymorphic CNVs in about 2,000 UK cases each of 8 common diseases, including rheumatoid arthritis, and about 3,000 shared controls, Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium et al. (2010) found a CNV in the HLA region associated with rheumatoid arthritis (CNVR2845.14; p = 1.4 x 10(-39); OR = 1.77). They had no evidence that the HLA CNVs associated with autoimmune diseases were signals independent of the known associated HLA haplotypes.
quotes: We observed CNVs in the HLA region associated variously with Crohn's disease (CNVR2841.20, p= 1.2 × 10−5, OR = 0.80), rheumatoid arthritis (CNVR2845.14, p= 1.4 × 10−39, OR = 1.77), and type 1 diabetes (CNVR2845.46, p= 8 × 10−153, OR = 0.2).
we have no evidence that suggests that the HLA CNVs associated with autoimmune diseases in this study represent signals independent of the known associated haplotypes.

findings.statement: Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium et al. (2010) found a CNV (CNVR1065.1) that is annotated as mapping uniquely to chromosome 2 and showed a strong association with rheumatoid arthritis (p = 6.8 x 10(-49); OR = 1.85) and type 1 diabetes. They showed it to be a dispersed duplication: the polymorphism is actually located in the HLA region and is well tagged by HLA SNPs known to be associated with both diseases.
quotes: We found one similar example, of a CNV (CNVR1065.1, featuring in Table 2 as a replicated association) annotated as mapping uniquely to chromosome 2 which shows a strong signal in type 1 diabetes and rheumatoid arthritis.
Careful examination shows it to be another dispersed duplication where the polymorphism is located in the HLA, and is well tagged by HLA SNPs known to be associated with both diseases.

findings.statement: Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium et al. (2010) also found that a novel HLA-region sequence insertion CNV (AC_000138.1_44) was associated with rheumatoid arthritis (p = 8.3 x 10(-4); OR = 0.87). The association replicated in 3,398 cases and 2,743 controls (replication p = 1.1 x 10(-3)).

Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium et al. (2010) found no formally significant evidence replicating the reported association between CCL3L1 copy number and rheumatoid arthritis (nominal p = 0.058). None of the multiallelic CNVs they tested (CCL3L1, beta-defensins, FCGR3A/B) was significantly associated with the 3 autoimmune diseases after correction for multiple testing.
quotes: None of the CNVs shows significant association with the three autoimmune diseases in our study after allowance for multiple testing. In particular, we do not see formally significant evidence to replicate the reported association for CCL3L1 and rheumatoid arthritis (nominal p = 0.058).

relevance_reason: Pathogenesis study showing platelet microparticles in RA synovial fluid that drive IL-1-dependent synoviocyte activation, plus mouse models implicating platelets and GPVI in inflammatory arthritis.

findings.statement: Boilard et al. (2010) used flow cytometry to find platelet microparticles (CD41-positive, submicrometer vesicles) in synovial fluid from all 20 patients with rheumatoid arthritis tested, averaging just under 2 x 10(5) per microliter. These microparticles were undetectable in 19 of 20 osteoarthritis synovial fluid samples. Platelet microparticles were also present in synovial fluid from patients with juvenile idiopathic arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, and gout. Microparticles from neutrophils, T cells, and macrophages were present in much smaller amounts.
quotes: We found on average just under 2 × 105 CD41+ MPs per microliter of SF from patients with RA (Fig. 1C). In contrast to RA SF, where MPs were present in all samples, CD41+ MPs were undetectable in 19 out of 20 osteoarthritis (OA) SF samples (Fig. 1C).
We also detected platelet MPs in other inflammatory arthritides (Fig. 1D).
MPs expressing neutrophil, T cell, or macrophage markers were present albeit in substantially smaller amounts than observed for platelet MPs in RA SF (Fig. 1E).

findings.statement: Boilard et al. (2010) found that platelet microparticles stimulated synovial fibroblasts to produce IL-6 and IL-8. This applied both to microparticles produced by collagen stimulation of platelets and to microparticles isolated from rheumatoid arthritis synovial fluid. The effect depended on IL-1: microparticles from mice lacking Il1a and Il1b, and fibroblasts lacking the IL-1 receptor, failed to produce the response. Blocking both IL-1-alpha and IL-1-beta was needed to fully neutralize the effect, and IL-1-alpha predominated in the microparticles. The authors suggested that this may help explain the limited effect of IL-1 blockade in RA.
quotes: incubation of MPs isolated from RA SF induced FLS to release substantial quantities of both cytokines (Fig. 4B and fig. S3).
Platelet MPs from RA SF expressed surface IL-lα, which as in murine MPs predominated over IL-lβ (fig. S4).
The observation that membrane-associated MP IL-1 is unusually difficult to antagonize (Fig. 4) may help to explain the limited effect of IL-1 blockade in RA

findings.statement: In the K/BxN serum-transfer mouse model of inflammatory arthritis, Boilard et al. (2010) found that depleting platelets markedly reduced arthritis, as measured by both clinical scores and histology. Arthritis was not affected by loss or blockade of thromboxane synthase, the thromboxane receptor, or GPIb.
quotes: We found that platelet-depleted mice exhibited a marked reduction in arthritis as assessed by clinical scoring and by histological analysis (Fig. 2, A and B). These findings demonstrate that platelets are required for inflammatory arthritis development in vivo.

findings.statement: Boilard et al. (2010) showed that the collagen receptor glycoprotein VI (GPVI) and the Fc receptor gamma chain were the main mediators of platelet microparticle release when platelets were co-cultured with fibroblast-like synoviocytes. After K/BxN serum transfer, arthritis was significantly reduced in Gp6-null mice. The authors noted that antagonizing GPVI could be a new therapeutic approach.
quotes: Using platelets lacking either FcR–γ-chain (Fcer1g−/−) or GPVI (Gp6−/−), we found that generation of MPs by primary FLS was mediated predominantly via this pathway (Fig. 3B).
Both clinical and histomorphometric assessment confirmed that arthritis in Gp6−/− mice was significantly reduced (Fig. 3, E and F).
Because mice or humans lacking GPVI remain healthy, antagonism of this receptor represents a novel therapeutic approach.

relevance_reason: A GWAS follow-up study that identifies new rheumatoid arthritis susceptibility loci (CD2/CD58, CD28, PRDM1) and replicates four more (TAGAP, PTPRC, TRAF6/RAG1, FCGR2A). This is association evidence about RA risk loci.

findings.statement: Raychaudhuri et al. (2009) took 370 SNPs from 179 independent loci with P < 0.001 in a published RA GWAS meta-analysis of 3,393 cases and 12,462 controls. They used GRAIL, a text-mining method, to score these loci for functional relationships to genes in 16 established RA loci, and 22 loci scored as significantly connected. They genotyped 22 representative SNPs in an independent set of 7,957 autoantibody-positive cases and 11,958 matched controls of European ancestry. Seven SNPs replicated at a Bonferroni-corrected threshold (P < 0.0023).
quotes: We identified 22 loci with a significant degree of functional connectivity. We genotyped 22 representative SNPs in an independent set of 7,957 cases and 11,958 matched controls.
More compellingly, 7 SNPs achieved a Bonferroni-corrected level of significance in replication (p<0.0023, z>2.83).
All individuals were self-described white and of European ancestry.

findings.statement: Raychaudhuri et al. (2009) confirmed an association of RA with rs11586238 on 1p13.1, near the CD2 and CD58 genes (replication P = 1.4 x 10(-6); overall P = 1.0 x 10(-9); OR 1.13 for the minor G allele). The SNP lies 50 kb upstream of the CD2 start site and is also near CD58 and IGSF2.
quotes: we observed the strongest associations at rs11586238 on 1p13.1 near the CD2 and CD58 genes (1.4×10−6 replication, 1.0×10−9 overall)
The rs11586238 SNP is 50 kb upstream of the CD2 start site, but is also near multiple other key immunological genes including CD58, and IGSF2.

findings.statement: Raychaudhuri et al. (2009) confirmed an association of RA with rs1980422 on 2q33.2, about 10 kb from the 3-prime UTR of CD28 (replication P = 4.7 x 10(-6); overall P = 1.3 x 10(-9); OR 1.13 for the minor C allele). There was minimal linkage disequilibrium with the known CTLA4-region RA risk SNP rs3087243, and conditional analysis showed that the two SNPs confer RA risk independently.
quotes: at rs1980422 on 2q33.2 near CD28 (4.7×10−6 replication, 1.3×10−9 overall)
There is minimal LD between these two SNPs (r2=0.04, D’=0.40); conditional analysis confirmed that the two SNPs independently confer RA risk

findings.statement: Raychaudhuri et al. (2009) confirmed an association of RA with rs548234 on 6q21, located 10 kb downstream of the PRDM1 transcript (replication P = 1.2 x 10(-5); overall P = 2.1 x 10(-8); OR 1.11 for the minor C allele). They noted that PRDM1 (BLIMP-1) is a transcription factor that regulates terminal differentiation of B cells into plasma cells, which implicates a new process in RA.
quotes: at rs548234 on 6q21 near PRDM1 (1.2×10−5 replication, 2.1×10−8 overall). Based on conservative estimates of genome-wide significance these represent confirmed RA risk alleles.
Our study has also implicated novel processes represented by PRDM1 (BLIMP-1), a transcription factor that regulates terminal differentiation of B-cells into immunoglobulin secreting plasma cells.

findings.statement: Raychaudhuri et al. (2009) found that four further loci replicated, but their combined association did not reach a conservative genome-wide threshold: rs394581 near TAGAP (6q25.3; overall P = 3.8 x 10(-7)), rs10919563 in a PTPRC intron (1q31.3; overall P = 6.7 x 10(-7)), rs540386 in a TRAF6 intron (11p12; overall P = 3.9 x 10(-6)), and rs12746613 near FCGR2A (1q23.3; overall P = 1.5 x 10(-5)). The authors considered these likely true RA loci but said further genotyping was needed.
quotes: We observed evidence of association at rs394581 on 6q25.3 near TAGAP (1.5×10−4 replication, 3.8×10−7 overall), rs10919563 on 1q31.3 within a PTPRC intron (2.6×10−4 replication, 6.7×10−7 overall), rs540386 on 11p12 within a TRAF6 intron (8.3×10−4 replication, 3.9×10−6 overall)

and rs12746613 on 1q23.3 near FCGR2A (2.2×10−3 replication, 1.5×10−5 overall). These SNP associations likely represent true RA loci, but additional genotyping will be necessary for definitive confirmation.

findings.statement: Raychaudhuri et al. (2009) found that the 7 replicated SNPs had consistent effects across all 14 collections, with no evidence of heterogeneity. They also found no significant epistatic interactions among the replicated SNPs and the known RA risk alleles.
quotes: our seven replicated SNP associations demonstrate consistent effects across all 14 collections without evidence of heterogeneity (p>0.05 by Breslow-Day test of Heterogeneity, see Table 2).
Despite the functional relationships between these genes, we found no evidence of significant interactions.

findings.statement: Raychaudhuri et al. (2009) noted that several of the new RA loci lie in regions already associated with other autoimmune diseases. These were FCGR2A (systemic lupus erythematosus), TAGAP (celiac disease and type 1 diabetes), PTPRC (multiple sclerosis), PRDM1 (Crohn disease) and CD58 (multiple sclerosis). The authors suggested that the loci point to T-cell activation, NF-kappa-B signaling, and B-cell activation and differentiation in RA pathogenesis.
quotes: Many of these seven alleles further implicate genomic regions already associated with autoimmune diseases (see Table 3).
These SNP associations continue to clarify critical biological processes involved in RA pathogenesis, including T-cell activation, NF-κB signaling, and B-cell activation and differentiation.

relevance_reason: Case-control gene-environment study showing that RA susceptibility depends on interaction between HLA-DRB1 shared epitope, PTPN22, smoking and autoantibodies to citrullinated alpha-enolase.

findings.statement: In 1,497 individuals from 3 RA cohorts, Mahdi et al. (2009) found antibodies to the immunodominant citrullinated alpha-enolase CEP-1 epitope in 43 to 63% of anti-CCP-positive individuals. This subset was preferentially linked to HLA-DRB1*04.
quotes: In 1,497 individuals from three RA cohorts, antibodies to the immunodominant citrullinated alpha-enolase CEP-1 epitope were detected in 43-63% of the anti-CCP-positive individuals, and this subset was preferentially linked to HLA-DRB1*04.

findings.statement: In a case-control analysis of 1,000 RA patients and 872 controls, Mahdi et al. (2009) found that the combined effect of HLA-DRB1 shared epitope alleles, PTPN22 and smoking was most strongly associated with the anti-CEP-1-positive subset of RA (odds ratio 37). The corresponding anti-CEP-1-negative, anti-CCP-positive subset had an odds ratio of 2. The authors concluded that citrullinated alpha-enolase is a specific citrullinated autoantigen that links smoking to genetic risk factors in the development of RA.
quotes: In a case-control analysis of 1,000 affected individuals and 872 controls, the combined effect of shared epitope, PTPN22 and smoking showed the strongest association with the anti-CEP-1-positive subset (odds ratio (OR) of 37, compared to an OR of 2 for the corresponding anti-CEP-1-negative, anti-CCP-positive subset).
We conclude that citrullinated alpha-enolase is a specific citrullinated autoantigen that links smoking to genetic risk factors in the development of RA.

relevance_reason: A genome-wide association study with replication that identifies REL on chromosome 2p13 as a rheumatoid arthritis susceptibility locus and confirms associations at CTLA4 and BLK.

findings.statement: Gregersen et al. (2009) carried out a genome-wide association study of rheumatoid arthritis in 2,418 cases and 4,504 controls of European origin from North America; about 95% of the cases were positive for anti-CCP antibodies. They found an association at the REL locus on chromosome 2p13 for rs13031237 (P = 6.01 x 10(-10)) and rs13017599 (P = 9.05 x 10(-9)). After PTPN22, this was the second most significant non-MHC signal. In replication sets of 2,604 cases and 2,882 controls from the US and Canada, the association was confirmed. In the combined data, the allelic OR was 1.25 for rs13031237 (P = 3.08 x 10(-14)) and 1.21 for rs13017599 (P = 2.60 x 10(-11)).
quotes: We conducted a genome-wide association study of rheumatoid arthritis in 2,418 cases and 4,504 controls from North America and identified an association at the REL locus, encoding c-Rel, on chromosome 2p13 (rs13031237, P = 6.01 x 10(-10)).

Replication in independent case-control datasets comprising 2,604 cases and 2,882 controls confirmed this association, yielding an allelic OR = 1.25 (P = 3.08 x 10(-14)) for marker rs13031237 and an allelic OR = 1.21 (P = 2.60 x 10(-11)) for marker rs13017599 in the combined dataset.

However, after PTPN22 the second most significant association is observed on chromosome 2 in the region of REL, where two markers provide highly significant evidence of association (rs13031237, allele specific p=6.01 × 10-10 and rs13017599, allele specific p=9.05 × 10-9), as shown in Table 1.
findings.population: North American of European origin (US and Canada)

findings.statement: In the combined dataset, Gregersen et al. (2009) also found definitive support for an association of rheumatoid arthritis with CTLA4 SNP rs231735 (OR = 0.85; P = 6.25 x 10(-9)), which had been suggested previously. The genotype-specific results showed codominant effects at all loci except CTLA4, where the effect was nearly dominant.
quotes: The combined dataset also provides definitive support for associations at both CTLA4 (rs231735; OR = 0.85; P = 6.25 x 10(-9)) and BLK (rs2736340; OR = 1.19; P = 5.69 x 10(-9)).
Supplementary table 4 presents genotype-specific results, which show codominance for all the loci except CTLA4, which is nearly dominant.

findings.statement: Gregersen et al. (2009) presented BLK as a new rheumatoid arthritis risk locus, with an association at rs2736340 in the combined dataset (OR = 1.19; P = 5.69 x 10(-9)). They noted that this locus had recently been associated with systemic lupus.
quotes: The data also support BLK as a new RA risk locus (rs2736340, OR 1.19, p=5.69 × 10-9), a finding of some interest given the recent association of this locus with systemic lupus,.

findings.statement: In the genome-wide scan, Gregersen et al. (2009) confirmed the previously reported associations with the MHC region (maximum P = 9.50 x 10(-104)), PTPN22 (rs2476601, P = 1.62 x 10(-21)) and the TRAF1/C5 region (rs881375, P = 4.09 x 10(-8)). Testing all pairwise interactions between SNPs in CTLA4, REL and BLK identified no significant gene-gene interaction after correction for multiple testing.
quotes: As noted in previous studies, the largest association signal is in an extended region within the MHC achieving a maximal level significance of p=9.50 × 10-104 in this study.
In addition, the previously reported associations are confirmed at PTPN22 (rs2476601, p= 1.62 × 10-21) and the TRAF1/C5 regions (maximal association at rs881375, p= 4.09×10-8).
Given that 471 tests were performed, no significant interaction effects were identified, after correcting for multiple testing.

findings.statement: Gregersen et al. (2009) suggested that the associations at CD40, REL, TRAF1 and TNFAIP3 point to an important role for CD40 signaling pathways in rheumatoid arthritis pathogenesis. They noted that c-Rel regulates T-cell genes including CD40 and TNFAIP3 and, like PRKCQ, is involved in the survival of activated CD8 cells.
quotes: The associations of CD40, REL, TRAF1 and TNFAIP3 are consistent with an important role for CD40 signaling pathways in RA pathogenesis.
In addition, a variety of genes in T cells are regulated by c-Rel, including CD40 and TNFAIP3, both of which are now accepted RA susceptibility loci.

findings.statement: Gregersen et al. (2009) noted that 50 to 80% of patients meeting standard criteria for rheumatoid arthritis have anti-CCP antibodies. The classical HLA-DRB1 associations, and many other reported genetic associations, are restricted to this subgroup. They also noted evidence for genetic heterogeneity in rheumatoid arthritis risk among racial groups.
quotes: between 50 and 80% of patients meeting standard criteria for RA exhibit anti-CCP antibodies. Remarkably, the classical HLA-DRB1 associations with RA are entirely restricted to this phenotypic subgroup, as are many of the other reported genetic associations.
In addition to this phenotypic heterogeneity, there is evidence for genetic heterogeneity in risk for RA among different racial groups, and this has complicated efforts at replication.

relevance_reason: Fine-mapping association study of the 6q23 (OLIG3/TNFAIP3) RA susceptibility locus in a large UK case-control cohort; identifies three independent associated SNPs and their combined effect.

findings.statement: Orozco et al. (2009) fine-mapped the 6q23 RA susceptibility locus by genotyping 70 SNPs in 3,962 UK RA patients of Northern European descent and 3,531 healthy controls, and found 18 SNPs associated with RA. The strongest association was with rs6920220 (P = 2.61 x 10(-7), OR 1.22), located in an intergenic region between OLIG3 and TNFAIP3, and haplotype 1, tagged by rs6920220, conferred risk for RA.
quotes: 3962 RA patients and 3531 healthy controls were included in the study. We found 18 SNPs associated with RA.
The SNPs showing the strongest association with RA remained rs6920220 [P = 2.61 × 10−7, OR (95% CI) 1.22 (1.13–1.32)]
All cases were Caucasian of Northern European descent and all fulfilled the 1987 American College of Rheumatology classification criteria modified for genetic studies.
findings.population: UK, Caucasian of Northern European descent

findings.statement: Orozco et al. (2009) found that the next most strongly associated SNP at 6q23 was rs13207033 (P = 0.0001, OR 0.86), which was perfectly correlated with rs10499194; the minor allele was protective. The authors stated that this was the first independent replication of the association of rs10499194 with RA susceptibility.
quotes: The next most strongly associated polymorphisms were the SNPs rs13207033 [P = 0.0001, OR (95% CI) 0.86 (0.80–0.93)], rs13192841 and rs1257282 all of which were perfectly correlated (r2 = 1) with rs10499194.
This represents the first independent replication of the association of the rs10499194 polymorphism with RA susceptibility.

findings.statement: Orozco et al. (2009) identified a new potential RA marker, rs5029937, in intron 2 of TNFAIP3. Conditional logistic regression showed that only rs6920220, rs13207033, and rs5029937 stayed significant, which suggests 3 independent effects. In pooled data with the WTCCC GWAS, rs5029937 remained highly significant after conditioning on both other SNPs (P = 7.59 x 10(-6)). The authors said replication in an independent cohort was needed.
quotes: Only three SNPs, rs6920220, rs13207033 and rs5029937, remained significant after conditioning on each associated marker (Table 2)
This polymorphism showed a highly significant association with RA after conditioning on rs6920220, rs13207033 and both (P-values 4.71 × 10−11, 6.95 × 10−6 and 7.59 × 10−6, respectively).
The results provide convincing evidence to support a third allele in the 6q23 region but replication in an independent cohort is required to confirm this unequivocally.

findings.statement: Orozco et al. (2009) found that carrying the risk alleles of both rs6920220 and rs5029937, together with absence of the protective allele of rs13207033, was strongly associated with RA compared with carrying none of them (OR 1.86). This equated to an effect size of 1.50 compared with controls, higher than for any single SNP. The high-risk combination was carried by 4.4% of patients and 2.3% of controls.
quotes: The combination of the carriage of both risk alleles of rs6920220 and rs5029937 together with the absence of the protective allele of rs13207033 was strongly associated with RA when compared with carriage of none [OR of 1.86 (95% CI) (1.51–2.29)].

This equates to an effect size of 1.50 (95% CI 1.21–1.85) compared with controls and is higher than that obtained for any SNP individually (4.4% of the RA patients versus 2.3% of the controls carried this high-risk combination).

findings.statement: Orozco et al. (2009) found that rs6920220 and rs5029937 appeared to be associated with autoantibody-positive RA, with strong association in both RF-positive and anti-CCP-positive cases. In contrast, rs13207033 was associated with both RF-positive and RF-negative cases but only with anti-CCP-negative cases. All 3 SNPs were associated in both male and female patients.
quotes: rs6920220 and the intron 2 SNP, rs5029937, appeared to be associated with auto-antibody positive cases, with strong association in both RF positive and anti-CCP positive cases.
In contrast, rs13207033 was associated with both RF positive and negative RA cases, but only anti-CCP negative cases.

findings.statement: Orozco et al. (2009) found that the functional exon 3 TNFAIP3 polymorphism rs2230926, which had been associated with SLE, was not independently associated with RA in their study.
quotes: Interestingly, this variant was not independently associated with RA in our study.

relevance_reason: Case-control association study that identifies AFF3 as a new RA susceptibility locus and replicates the CTLA4 and 4q27 (IL2/IL21) associations.

findings.statement: Barton et al. (2009) genotyped 18 SNPs at 14 loci previously suggested to be type 1 diabetes susceptibility loci in 3,962 UK RA cases and 3,531 unrelated UK controls. They identified an association between RA and SNP rs10865035 at the AFF3 locus on chromosome 2. Combined with WTCCC data (proxy SNP rs9653442) and an inception cohort, the analysis included 6,819 RA cases and 12,650 controls and gave OR 1.12 (95% CI 1.07-1.17), P = 2.8 x 10(-7). The associated variants map to the 5-prime and promoter region of AFF3, which is preferentially expressed in lymphoid cells.
quotes: Eighteen single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) mapping to 14 distinct loci were genotyped in 3962 UK RA cases and 3531 unrelated UK controls.
Hence, a combined analysis across all samples was undertaken and confirmed strong evidence for association of this locus with RA susceptibility (OR 1.12 95% CI 1.07–1.17, P = 2.8 × 10−7).
The associated variants map to the 5′ and promoter region of the AFF3 gene, which is strongly conserved in evolution and is preferentially expressed in lymphoid cells.
findings.population: UK, Caucasian of Northern European descent

findings.statement: Barton et al. (2009) replicated the association between RA and SNP rs3087243 in the 3-prime region of CTLA4 (OR 0.87, 95% CI 0.82-0.94, P = 1.1 x 10(-4)). In a meta-analysis that combined their data with 2 previous well-powered studies, the association was confirmed (OR 0.88, P = 2.6 x 10(-6)).
quotes: A variant mapping to the CTLA-4 gene showed the strongest evidence for association with RA in the current cohort (rs3087243 OR 0.87, 95% CI 0.82–0.94, P = 1.1 × 10−4).
Combining the results from two previous well-powered studies with the current data, the SNP is confirmed as being associated with RA susceptibility [OR 0.88 (0.83–0.93), P = 2.6 × 10−6] (Fig. 1).

findings.statement: Barton et al. (2009) replicated the association between RA and SNP rs6822844 in the IL2-IL21 region on chromosome 4q27. As reported before, the common allele predisposed to disease (OR 0.86, 95% CI 0.79-0.94, P = 5.4 x 10(-4)).
quotes: As reported previously, it was the common allele that predisposed to disease [rs6822844 OR 0.86, (0.79–0.94), P = 5.4 × 10−4].

findings.statement: Barton et al. (2009) stratified RA patients by rheumatoid factor and anti-CCP autoantibody status. At the AFF3, CTLA4 and IL2/IL21 SNPs, the strength of association was similar in autoantibody-positive and autoantibody-negative patients.
quotes: However, following stratification by presence of auto-antibodies, the strength of associations was similar between auto-antibody positive and negative individuals at all three SNPs indicated by the overlapping confidence intervals (Table 2).

findings.statement: Barton et al. (2009) found that the common allele of the nonsynonymous IL7R SNP rs6897932 was somewhat overrepresented in RA cases (OR 0.90, P = 0.007), but this trend did not reach significance after correction for multiple testing. They noted that a total of 13 RA susceptibility loci had now been confirmed.
quotes: Finally, although the common allele of a non-synonymous SNP (rs6897932) mapping to the IL7R gene previously associated with both T1D and multiple sclerosis was somewhat over-represented in RA cases (OR 0.90, 95% CI 0.84–0.97; trend P = 0.007), this did not achieve statistical significance at the corrected P-value threshold.
a total of 13 loci have now been confirmed as associated with RA susceptibility (HLA DRB1, PTPN22, STAT4, TRAF1/C5, 6q23, IL2RB, 12q13, 10p15, CD40, MMEL1, AFF3, 4q27 and CTLA-4).

relevance_reason: Association study that identifies CD244 functional SNPs as a susceptibility factor for rheumatoid arthritis in Japanese cohorts, with functional expression assays.

findings.statement: Suzuki et al. (2008) identified a linkage disequilibrium block associated with rheumatoid arthritis in the chromosome 1q region containing multiple SLAM family genes. Within this block, the association peaked at two functional SNPs in CD244, rs3766379 and rs6682654, in two independent rheumatoid arthritis cohorts from Japan (P = 3.23 x 10(-8) and P = 7.45 x 10(-8)).
quotes: We identified a linkage disequilibrium block associated with rheumatoid arthritis in the chromosome 1q region containing multiple SLAM family genes.
In this block, the association peaked at two functional SNPs (rs3766379 and rs6682654) in CD244 in two independent rheumatoid arthritis cohorts from Japan (P = 3.23 x 10(-8) and P = 7.45 x 10(-8)).

findings.statement: Suzuki et al. (2008) demonstrated that the rheumatoid arthritis-susceptible alleles of the CD244 SNPs rs3766379 and rs6682654, and their haplotype, increased expression in luciferase and allele-specific transcript quantification assays. The authors concluded that CD244 is a genetic risk factor for rheumatoid arthritis.
quotes: We demonstrated that the rheumatoid arthritis-susceptible alleles of rs3766379 and rs6682654 and their haplotype increased their expression in luciferase and allele-specific transcript quantification assays.
CD244 is a genetic risk factor for rheumatoid arthritis and may have a role in the autoimmune process shared by rheumatoid arthritis and systemic lupus erythematosus.

findings.statement: Suzuki et al. (2008) found that a Japanese cohort with systemic lupus erythematosus had a CD244 genotype distribution similar to that of the rheumatoid arthritis cohorts. They suggested that CD244 may have a role in the autoimmune process shared by rheumatoid arthritis and systemic lupus erythematosus.
quotes: We also identified a Japanese cohort with systemic lupus erythematosus that had a similar genotype distribution as the rheumatoid arthritis cohorts.
CD244 is a genetic risk factor for rheumatoid arthritis and may have a role in the autoimmune process shared by rheumatoid arthritis and systemic lupus erythematosus.

relevance_reason: A genome-wide association meta-analysis with replication that identified rheumatoid arthritis susceptibility loci at CD40, CCL21 and four other regions in people of European ancestry.

findings.statement: Raychaudhuri et al. (2008) carried out a meta-analysis of two published genome-wide association studies of rheumatoid arthritis (3,393 cases and 12,462 controls of European ancestry, from the WTCCC, EIRA and NARAC collections). They then genotyped 31 top-ranked SNPs not previously associated with rheumatoid arthritis in an independent replication set of 3,929 autoantibody-positive cases and 5,807 matched controls from 8 collections. Six of the 31 SNPs reached P of 0.01 or less in replication, which was significantly more than expected by chance.
quotes: we conducted a meta-analysis of two published genome-wide association (GWA) studies totaling 3,393 cases and 12,462 controls. We genotyped 31 top-ranked SNPs not previously associated with rheumatoid arthritis in an independent replication of 3,929 autoantibody-positive rheumatoid arthritis cases and 5,807 matched controls from eight separate collections.
In replication genotyping, we observed that 6 out of 31 SNPs obtained P ≤ 0.01; this is significantly more than expected by chance alone (P = 9 × 10−7 by Poisson).
findings.population: European ancestry (UK, Sweden, North America, Netherlands)

findings.statement: Raychaudhuri et al. (2008) identified an association between rheumatoid arthritis and SNP rs4810485 at chromosome 20q13, located in the second intron of the CD40 gene (overall P = 8.2 x 10(-9); replication P = 0.0032; odds ratio 0.87 for the minor T allele). rs4810485 is in near-perfect linkage disequilibrium (r2 = 0.95) with rs1883832, a variant that has been associated with autoimmune thyroid disease and has been shown to affect the efficiency of CD40 protein translation by disrupting a Kozak sequence. The same allele contributes to risk in both diseases.
quotes: We identified a common variant at the CD40 gene locus (rs4810485, P = 0.0032 replication, P = 8.2 x 10(-9) overall, OR = 0.87).
This SNP is located in the second intron of CD40 and is within an LD block that contains a large portion of the CD40 gene and its 5′ intergenic region.

A SNP in near-perfect LD with rs4810485 (r2 = 0.95, rs1883832) has been associated with autoimmune thyroid disease, although the association has not been confirmed unequivocally. The same allele contributes to risk in both diseases.

findings.statement: Raychaudhuri et al. (2008) identified an association between rheumatoid arthritis and SNP rs2812378 at chromosome 9p13, located about 0.1 kb from the 5-prime untranslated region of CCL21 (replication P = 0.00097; overall P = 2.8 x 10(-7); joint odds ratio 1.12). The SNP lies in a linkage disequilibrium block that includes the whole CCL21 coding sequence but not the nearby genes. CCL21 is a chemokine involved in homing lymphocytes to secondary lymphoid organs.
quotes: We also identified association at the CCL21 gene locus (rs2812378, P = 0.00097 replication, P = 2.8 x 10(-7) overall), a gene involved in lymphocyte trafficking.

The SNP is located ~0.1 kb from the 5′ untranslated region of the CCL21 gene, and is near a cluster of other genes including CCL19 and CCL27. However, it is in an LD block that fully includes the CCL21 coding sequence and not the other genes.

findings.statement: Raychaudhuri et al. (2008) found evidence of association between rheumatoid arthritis and 4 further loci: MMEL1-TNFRSF14 on 1p36 (rs3890745; overall P = 1.1 x 10(-7)), CDK6 on 7q21 (rs42041; overall P = 4.0 x 10(-6)), PRKCQ on 10p15 (rs4750316; overall P = 4.4 x 10(-6)), and KIF5A-PIP4K2C on 12q13 (rs1678542; overall P = 8.8 x 10(-8)). The authors stated that additional validation in large sample collections was required.
quotes: MMEL1-TNFRSF14 (rs3890745, P = 0.0035 replication, P = 1.1 x 10(-7) overall), CDK6 (rs42041, P = 0.010 replication, P = 4.0 x 10(-6) overall), PRKCQ (rs4750316, P = 0.0078 replication, P = 4.4 x 10(-6) overall), and KIF5A-PIP4K2C (rs1678542, P = 0.0026 replication, P = 8.8 x 10(-8) overall)

Most of the four other SNPs with P ≤ 0.01 in our combined stage 1 and 2 genotyping probably represent true rheumatoid arthritis susceptibility alleles, although additional validation in large sample collections is required.

findings.statement: In their genome-wide association meta-analysis, Raychaudhuri et al. (2008) observed association at the previously confirmed rheumatoid arthritis risk loci PTPN22, 6q23 (TNFAIP3), STAT4 and TRAF1-C5. They also observed association at 4q27 (IL2/IL21), which they described as an independent replication, and at CTLA4, but not at PADI4.
quotes: Of the confirmed non-MHC risk loci, we observed association at PTPN22, 6q23/(containing TNFAIP3), STAT4 and TRAF1-C5. We also observed evidence of association at 4q27 (containing the IL2 and IL21 genes) and CTLA4, but not PADI4.
CTLA4 replicates in the WTCCC (P = 0.026), providing further support for the role of this locus in rheumatoid arthritis

findings.statement: Raychaudhuri et al. (2008) concluded that the association at CD40, together with the associations near TRAF1 and TNFAIP3, gave strong evidence for a central role of the CD40 signaling pathway in autoantibody-positive rheumatoid arthritis. They suggested that this pathway may act through NF-kappa-B activation, and noted that CD40 stimulation drives B-cell proliferation by regulating CDK6 expression.
quotes: These associations provide strong evidence for the importance of the CD40 signaling pathway in autoantibody-positive rheumatoid arthritis. Our study implicates a putative functional variant that affects protein translation of the CD40 receptor.
Furthermore, CD40 stimulation results in B-cell proliferation through regulation of CDK6 expression.

findings.statement: Raychaudhuri et al. (2008) estimated that the newly identified variants together explained only 0.6% of the variance in rheumatoid arthritis risk, and that all known non-MHC common variants explained 3.6%. Given that about 60% of rheumatoid arthritis risk is thought to be genetic, with one-third of that from the MHC, they concluded that less than half of the genetic variation is explained by known risk alleles. They suggested that further common alleles of modest effect remain to be found.
quotes: Even under the assumption that all of these variants are true risk factors, their total percent variance explained is only 0.6% (Supplementary Note). In this study, we estimate that the total percent variance explained for all known non-MHC common genetic variants is just 3.6%.

Considering that ~60% of rheumatoid arthritis risk is thought to be genetic, and one-third of this risk is from the MHC locus, this indicates that less than half of genetic variation can be explained by the known rheumatoid arthritis risk alleles.

relevance_reason: Replicates the association of STAT4 rs7574865 with rheumatoid arthritis in a Spanish case-control cohort.

findings.statement: Martínez et al. (2008) genotyped the STAT4 tagging polymorphism rs7574865 by TaqMan assay in 575 Spanish patients with rheumatoid arthritis and 723 ethnically matched healthy controls. They confirmed the association with RA (T vs G allele, P = 1.2 x 10(-6); odds ratio 1.59, 95% CI 1.31-1.92).
quotes: The association of STAT4 polymorphism rs7574865 with RA was validated in patients of Spanish origin (for T versus G, P = 1.2 x 10(-6), odds ratio [OR] 1.59, 95% confidence interval [95% CI] 1.31-1.92)
575 with RA, 440 with multiple sclerosis, 700 with inflammatory bowel disease, 311 with type 1 diabetes, and 723 ethnically matched healthy control subjects

findings.statement: In the same Spanish cohort, Martínez et al. (2008) also found an association of STAT4 rs7574865 with inflammatory bowel disease, covering both Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis (T vs G, P = 0.006; OR 1.29). They also found an association with type 1 diabetes (P = 0.008; OR 1.36). They found no association with multiple sclerosis (P = 0.83). The authors concluded that STAT4 is emerging as a common risk factor for diverse complex diseases.
quotes: the association was described for the first time in both clinical forms of inflammatory bowel disease, Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis (for T versus G, P = 0.006, OR 1.29, 95% CI 1.07-1.55), and in type 1 diabetes mellitus (for T versus G, P = 0.008, OR 1.36, 95% CI 1.07-1.71)
the genotypic distribution of this polymorphism showed no difference between patients with multiple sclerosis and healthy control subjects (for T versus G, P = 0.83, OR 1.02, 95% CI 0.82-1.28)
The STAT4 gene is emerging as a novel common risk factor for diverse complex diseases.

relevance_reason: A genome-wide association study with replication that found two independent susceptibility SNPs for rheumatoid arthritis at 6q23, near TNFAIP3 and OLIG3.

findings.statement: Plenge et al. (2007) genotyped 397 individuals with rheumatoid arthritis for 116,204 SNPs. They compared these data with publicly available genotype data for 1,211 related individuals from the Framingham Heart Study. After adjusting for technical and population biases, they found a SNP at 6q23 (rs10499194), about 150 kb from TNFAIP3 and OLIG3, that was reproducibly associated with rheumatoid arthritis. The association was seen in the GWA scan (P = 10(-3)) and in 5,541 additional case-control samples (P < 10(-6)), giving a combined P of 10(-9).
quotes: we genotyped 397 individuals with rheumatoid arthritis for 116,204 SNPs and carried out an association analysis in comparison to publicly available genotype data for 1,211 related individuals from the Framingham Heart Study

we identified a SNP at 6q23 (rs10499194, approximately 150 kb from TNFAIP3 and OLIG3) that was reproducibly associated with rheumatoid arthritis both in the genome-wide association (GWA) scan and in 5,541 additional case-control samples (P = 10(-3), GWA scan; P < 10(-6), replication; P = 10(-9), combined)

findings.statement: Plenge et al. (2007) noted that the Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium (WTCCC) had reported an association between rheumatoid arthritis and a different SNP, rs6920220, located 3.8 kb from rs10499194. Plenge et al. (2007) showed that the two SNP associations were statistically independent and were each reproducible when their data were compared with the WTCCC data. Together, the two SNPs defined risk and protective haplotypes for rheumatoid arthritis at 6q23.
quotes: the Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium (WTCCC) has reported strong association of rheumatoid arthritis susceptibility to a different SNP located 3.8 kb from rs10499194 (rs6920220; P = 5 x 10(-6) in WTCCC)

We show that these two SNP associations are statistically independent, are each reproducible in the comparison of our data and WTCCC data, and define risk and protective haplotypes for rheumatoid arthritis at 6q23.

relevance_reason: Validation study that confirmed a new rheumatoid arthritis susceptibility locus at 6q23 (rs6920220, between OLIG3 and TNFAIP3) and reported subphenotype associations.

findings.statement: Thomson et al. (2007) genotyped 9 SNPs that the WTCCC genome-wide association screen had putatively associated with rheumatoid arthritis (P = 1 x 10(-5) to 5 x 10(-7)) in an independent UK cohort of 5,063 RA cases and 3,849 healthy controls. One SNP, rs6920220 (G>A), was replicated (OR for the minor allele = 1.23; 95% CI 1.15-1.33; trend P = 1.1 x 10(-8)). In a combined analysis with the WTCCC data, the trend P value was 3.6 x 10(-12) (OR = 1.22). The SNP maps to an intergenic region of 6q23, between the OLIG3 and TNFAIP3 genes.
quotes: SNPs at these loci were genotyped in an independent cohort of 5,063 rheumatoid arthritis cases and 3,849 healthy controls

Of the nine newly identified SNPs tested, rs6920220 (G > A) showed association with rheumatoid arthritis in this cohort (OR for minor allele = 1.23, 95% CI = 1.15-1.33, trend P = 1.1 × 10-8) (Table 1).
we obtained strong statistical evidence for association between this SNP and rheumatoid arthritis (OR = 1.22, 95% CI = 1.15-1.29, trend P = 3.6 × 10-12) (Table 1).

findings.statement: Thomson et al. (2007) found that rs6920220 lies in a 60-kb linkage disequilibrium block that contains no known genes but includes part of a PTPN11 pseudogene. The block lies between OLIG3 and TNFAIP3 (A20). The authors noted that TNFAIP3 negatively regulates NF-kappa-B and that TNFAIP3-deficient mice develop multiorgan inflammation, including inflammation of the joints.
quotes: all five SNPs map to a single linkage-disequilibrium block spanning 60 kb
The block contains no known genes or transcripts but does encompass part of the PTPN11 pseudogene.
Mice deficient for the TNFAIP3 protein developed multiorgan inflammation, including inflammation of joints.

findings.statement: Thomson et al. (2007) found that the rs6920220 association was stronger in RA patients with antibodies to cyclic citrullinated peptide (anti-CCP) and in rheumatoid factor-positive patients. In the WTCCC data, the OR was 1.38 in anti-CCP-positive patients and 1.03 in anti-CCP-negative patients. In the combined cohorts, the difference between the anti-CCP-positive and -negative subgroups was significant (trend P = 0.003). The authors suggested that RA may comprise at least 2 genetically distinct subsets.
quotes: Analysis of the WTCCC study indicated a significant association for SNP rs6920220 in anti-CCP-positive (OR = 1.38, 95% CI = 1.22-1.55, trend P = 1.7 × 10-7) but not in anti-CCP-negative individuals (OR = 1.03, 95% CI = 0.82-1.29).
Indeed, the difference between the anti-CCP-positive and negative subgroups was statistically significant (trend P = 0.003).
the clinical phenotype of rheumatoid arthritis may actually comprise at least two genetically distinct subsets

findings.statement: Thomson et al. (2007) found no interaction between rs6920220 and the HLA-DRB1 or PTPN22 susceptibility markers, suggesting that this variant has an independent effect. Together, the HLA-DRB1 shared epitope, PTPN22 rs2476601, and rs6920220 accounted for 8.5% of the total variance in RA susceptibility. The PTPN22 rs2476601 association was also confirmed in this cohort (OR = 1.53; trend P = 2.0 x 10(-18)).
quotes: We did not detect evidence for interaction with HLA-DRB1 or PTPN22 susceptibility markers, suggesting that the rs6920220 variant confers an additional effect independent of the two known susceptibility genes.
Together, HLA-DRB1 (shared epitope), PTPN22 (rs2476601) and rs6920220 account for 8.5% of the total variance in rheumatoid arthritis susceptibility.
We detected strong association with the rheumatoid arthritis-causing SNP in the PTPN22 gene (rs2476601), as expected (odds ratio (OR) = 1.53, 95% CI = 1.39-1.68, trend P = 2.0 × 10-18).

findings.statement: Thomson et al. (2007) found modest evidence of association with RA for rs743777 in IL2RB (combined trend P = 5.3 x 10(-6); OR = 1.13). Evidence for the reported sex-differentiated effect of rs11761231 near PODXL was only borderline (trend P = 0.042). The IL2RA SNP rs2104286 was not associated with RA in this dataset.
quotes: In the combined cohort analysis, this SNP showed modest evidence for association (OR = 1.13, 95% CI = 1.07-1.19; trend P = 5.3 × 10-6), suggesting the effect, if any, is weak.
The present study provided only borderline evidence (trend P = 0.042) to support this observation

Notably, rs2104286, which maps to IL2RA, a gene already associated with a number of other autoimmune diseases (type 1 diabetes, multiple sclerosis and Graves’ disease) and known to play a role in T cell regulation, was not associated with rheumatoid arthritis in this dataset.

relevance_reason: Case-control association study identifying a STAT4 haplotype (rs7574865) associated with susceptibility to rheumatoid arthritis, mapped within the chromosome 2q linkage region.

findings.statement: Remmers et al. (2007) tested SNPs in and around 13 candidate genes within the previously linked chromosome 2q region for association with rheumatoid arthritis, then performed fine mapping of the STAT1-STAT4 region in 1,620 North American patients with established rheumatoid arthritis and 2,635 controls.
quotes: We tested single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in and around 13 candidate genes within the previously linked chromosome 2q region for association with rheumatoid arthritis.
We then performed fine mapping of the STAT1-STAT4 region in a total of 1620 case patients with established rheumatoid arthritis and 2635 controls, all from North America.

findings.statement: Remmers et al. (2007) found that a SNP haplotype in the third intron of STAT4, marked by rs7574865, was associated with susceptibility to rheumatoid arthritis: the minor alleles were present on 27% of chromosomes of North American patients with established RA vs 22% of controls (P = 2.81 x 10(-7); odds ratio 1.32). The association was replicated in an independent Swedish series of 1,529 patients with early (recent-onset) RA and 881 matched controls (P = 0.02).
quotes: A SNP haplotype in the third intron of STAT4 was associated with susceptibility to both rheumatoid arthritis and systemic lupus erythematosus.

The minor alleles of the haplotype-defining SNPs were present in 27% of chromosomes of patients with established rheumatoid arthritis, as compared with 22% of those of controls (for the SNP rs7574865, P=2.81x10(-7); odds ratio for having the risk allele in chromosomes of patients vs. those of controls, 1.32).
