The association was replicated in Swedish patients with recent-onset rheumatoid arthritis (P=0.02) and matched controls.

findings.statement: Remmers et al. (2007) reported that homozygosity for the STAT4 risk allele, compared with absence of the allele, was associated with a 60% increased risk for rheumatoid arthritis and a more than doubled risk for systemic lupus erythematosus.
quotes: Homozygosity of the risk allele, as compared with absence of the allele, was associated with a more than doubled risk for lupus and a 60% increased risk for rheumatoid arthritis.

findings.statement: Remmers et al. (2007) found that the STAT4 haplotype marked by rs7574865 was also strongly associated with systemic lupus erythematosus in 1,039 patients and 1,248 controls from 3 series (31% vs 22% of chromosomes; P = 1.87 x 10(-9); odds ratio 1.55), suggesting a shared pathway for rheumatoid arthritis and SLE.
quotes: The haplotype marked by rs7574865 was strongly associated with lupus, being present on 31% of chromosomes of case patients and 22% of those of controls (P=1.87x10(-9); odds ratio for having the risk allele in chromosomes of patients vs. those of controls, 1.55).
A haplotype of STAT4 is associated with increased risk for both rheumatoid arthritis and systemic lupus erythematosus, suggesting a shared pathway for these illnesses.

relevance_reason: A genomewide association study that finds TRAF1-C5 on chromosome 9 to be a susceptibility locus for anti-CCP-positive rheumatoid arthritis.

findings.statement: Plenge et al. (2007) performed a genomewide association study of 317,503 SNPs in 1,522 anti-CCP-positive rheumatoid arthritis cases and 1,850 matched controls. Samples came from the North American Rheumatoid Arthritis Consortium (NARAC) and the Swedish EIRA study. SNPs with P<1x10(-8) were then genotyped in an independent replication set of 997 cases and 1,777 controls. In all samples tested, they observed association with the MHC locus, with PTPN22, and with SNP rs3761847 on chromosome 9 (odds ratio 1.32; 95% CI 1.23-1.42; P = 4 x 10(-14)).
quotes: We genotyped 317,503 single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in a combined case-control study of 1522 case subjects with rheumatoid arthritis and 1850 matched control subjects.

We observed associations between disease and variants in the major-histocompatibility-complex locus, in PTPN22, and in a SNP (rs3761847) on chromosome 9 for all samples tested, the latter with an odds ratio of 1.32 (95% confidence interval, 1.23 to 1.42; P=4x10(-14)).

findings.statement: Plenge et al. (2007) found that the associated SNP rs3761847 is in linkage disequilibrium with 2 genes relevant to chronic inflammation: TRAF1 (tumor necrosis factor receptor-associated factor 1) and C5 (complement component 5). They concluded that a common genetic variant at the TRAF1-C5 locus on chromosome 9 is associated with an increased risk of anti-CCP-positive rheumatoid arthritis.
quotes: The SNP is in linkage disequilibrium with two genes relevant to chronic inflammation: TRAF1 (encoding tumor necrosis factor receptor-associated factor 1) and C5 (encoding complement component 5).
A common genetic variant at the TRAF1-C5 locus on chromosome 9 is associated with an increased risk of anti-CCP-positive rheumatoid arthritis.

relevance_reason: Genetic association study linking IRF5 promoter haplotype to RA susceptibility, mainly anti-CCP-negative RA.

findings.statement: Sigurdsson et al. (2007) analyzed 5 SNPs in IRF5 and 3 SNPs in TYK2 in a Swedish cohort of 1,530 patients with rheumatoid arthritis and 881 controls. Four of the 5 SNPs in the 5-prime region of IRF5 were associated with RA, whereas no association was observed with the TYK2 SNPs. The minor alleles of 3 IRF5 SNPs, which were in linkage disequilibrium and formed a relatively common haplotype (frequency approximately 0.33), appeared to confer protection against RA.
quotes: Five single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in IRF5 and 3 SNPs in Tyk2 were analyzed in a Swedish cohort of 1,530 patients with RA and 881 controls.
Four of the 5 SNPs located in the 5' region of IRF5 were associated with RA, while no association was observed with the Tyk2 SNPs.

The minor alleles of 3 of the IRF5 SNPs, which were in linkage disequilibrium and formed a relatively common haplotype with a frequency of approximately 0.33, appeared to confer protection against RA.

findings.statement: Sigurdsson et al. (2007) found that the IRF5 associations with RA were seen in the entire patient group but were mainly found in patients negative for anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide (anti-CCP) antibodies; a suggestive association of IRF5 SNPs with anti-CCP-negative RA was also observed in a Dutch replication cohort of 387 patients and 181 controls. The authors concluded that IRF5 variants contribute to a unique disease etiology and pathogenesis in anti-CCP-negative RA.
quotes: Although these disease associations were seen in the entire patient group, they were mainly found in RA patients who were negative for anti-CCP.
A replication study was performed in a Dutch cohort of 387 patients with RA and 181 controls.
our results indicate that genetic variants of IRF5 contribute to a unique disease etiology and pathogenesis in anti-CCP-negative RA.

relevance_reason: A genome-wide association study that includes about 2,000 British rheumatoid arthritis cases. It confirmed the HLA-DRB1 and PTPN22 associations and reported new or suggestive RA loci: a female-specific signal on 7q32 and signals at IL2RA, IL2RB, PTPN2, 12q24 and 6q23.

findings.statement: In a genome-wide association study of about 2,000 British Caucasian patients with rheumatoid arthritis and 3,000 shared controls typed with the Affymetrix 500K chip, Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium (2007) confirmed strong association with the MHC/HLA-DRB1 region on chromosome 6p21. The strongest MHC SNP was rs6457617 (trend P = 3.44 x 10(-76)). The cases met the 1987 American College of Rheumatology criteria.
quotes: An association between RA and alleles of the HLA-DRB1 locus has long been established.
Both these previous associations emerge strongly here (Table 2).

findings.statement: Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium (2007) found strong association between rheumatoid arthritis and the PTPN22 SNP rs6679677 on chromosome 1p13 (trend P = 4.9 x 10(-26); heterozygote OR 1.98, homozygote OR 3.32). This SNP is perfectly correlated (HapMap CEU r2 = 1) with the functional SNP rs2476601, and the effect size agreed with previous estimates. The authors noted that the HLA-DRB1 and PTPN22 associations together explain about 50% of the familial aggregation of RA.
quotes: The most associated marker within PTPN22 (rs6679677: chromosome 1p13) is perfectly correlated (HapMap CEU data r2=1) with the functionally relevant SNP (rs2476601) described previously, and the effect size is consistent with previous estimates.
These known associations with HLA-DRB1 and PTPN22 explain around 50% of the familial aggregation of RA.

findings.statement: Among the seven diseases studied, rheumatoid arthritis was the only one for which a sex-differentiated analysis produced a strong signal. Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium (2007) found that SNP rs11761231 on chromosome 7q32 gave P = 3.9 x 10(-7) on the 2-df sex-differentiated test. The SNP had no effect in males (P = 0.68) but an additive effect in females (P = 6.8 x 10(-8); OR 1.32). The authors advised caution because the SNP is surrounded by recombination hotspots and has no correlated SNPs on the chip, and they suggested it may represent one of the first sex-differentiated effects in human disease.
quotes: The SNP rs11761231 (chromosome 7) generates a P value of 3.9×10-7 for the 2-degrees of freedom (d.f.) sex-differentiated test which combines trend tests in males and females (Table 3).

This genotype has no effect on disease status in males, but a strong apparently additive effect in females (P value in a logistic regression model with additive log-odds is 0.68 in males and 6.8×10-8 in females, additive OR for females 1.32), and may represent one of the first sex-differentiated effects in human diseases.

Some caution is therefore required, but this represents a potentially interesting finding which warrants further investigation, particularly given the sex-related prevalence difference characteristic of this condition.

findings.statement: Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium (2007) found moderate evidence (P between 10(-5) and 5 x 10(-7)) of rheumatoid arthritis association at 9 SNPs, none of which lay at previously reported RA loci. These included SNPs near IL2RA (rs2104286) and IL2RB (rs743777). When RA and type 1 diabetes cases were combined, the IL2RA/CD25 region on 10p15 reached P = 5 x 10(-8).
quotes: None of the 9 SNPs with nominal P values in the range 10-5 to 5×10-7 (Table 4) map to loci previously associated with RA. Of particular interest is the association of SNPs mapping close to both the alpha and beta chains of the IL2 receptor (rs2104286 in the case of IL2RA; rs743777 and IL2RB).

The CD25 region has previously been shown to be associated with Graves’ disease and the present study also provides evidence of association with RA (combined trend test P=5×10-8, P=~7×10-6 for RA and T1D separately, Supplementary Table 11).

findings.statement: Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium (2007) reported data that add variants around IL2RA (10p15), PTPN2 (18p11) and the 12q24 region to the loci shared by rheumatoid arthritis and type 1 diabetes. All three appeared to be new for RA. At PTPN2 the RA association was weak (P = 1.9 x 10(-2)), but the combined P value for Crohn disease, RA and type 1 diabetes was 9 x 10(-8). The 12q24 variant gave a combined P value of 9.3 x 10(-10) across all autoimmune cases.
quotes: As detailed elsewhere, our study provides data indicating that this list can be extended to include variants around IL2RA (chromosome 10p15), PTPN2 (chromosome 18p11) and the chromosome 12q24 region (Supplementary Table 11), all apparently novel in RA.

The same locus also shows strong association with T1D susceptibility (trend test P=1.9×10-6) and a consistent, though weaker, association with RA (P=1.9×10-2), supporting the existence of overlapping pathways in the pathogenesis of very distinct inflammatory phenotypes
Indeed, the 12q24 variant most associated with T1D also features in both the CD and RA scans, generating a combined signal for all autoimmune cases of 9.3×10-10 (Supplementary Table 11).

findings.statement: Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium (2007) found moderate evidence of rheumatoid arthritis association at SNP rs6920220 on 6q23 (trend P = 4.99 x 10(-6)). Weaker signals (P between 10(-4) and 10(-5)) were seen in TNFAIP2 (rs2771369), GZMB (rs854350), PRKCQ (rs4750316) and KAZALD1 (rs10786617); the authors suggested that KAZALD1 might be relevant to bone erosions in RA. Two CTLA4 SNPs were only nominally significant (P = 0.085 and 0.034).
quotes: Examples include SNPs within genes implicated in the TNF pathway (for example, rs2771369 in TNFAIP2 (tumour necrosis factor, alpha-induced protein 2)) or in the regulation of T-cell function (rs854350 in GZMB (granzyme B) and rs4750316 in PRKCQ (protein kinase C, theta)).
two SNPs mapping to CTLA-4 (cytotoxic T-lymphocyte associated 4) rs3087243 and rs11571300 were only nominally significant (P=0.085 and P=0.034, respectively)

relevance_reason: A case-control study of gene-gene and gene-environment interactions involving HLA-DRB1 shared epitope alleles, PTPN22 R620W and smoking in rheumatoid arthritis.

findings.statement: Kallberg et al. (2007) studied interaction between HLA-DRB1 shared epitope (SE) alleles and the PTPN22 R620W allele in 3 case-control studies: the Swedish EIRA, the North American NARAC, and the Dutch Leiden Early Arthritis Clinic study, totaling 1,977 cases and 2,405 controls. When interaction was defined as departure from additivity, all 3 studies showed consistent interaction between HLA-DRB1 SE alleles and the A allele of PTPN22 R620W for anti-CCP-positive RA. A multiplicative interaction was seen only when the 3 studies were pooled. The linkage disequilibrium approach indicated gene-gene interaction in EIRA and NARAC and in the pooled analysis.
quotes: in three large case-control studies: the Swedish Epidemiological Investigation of Rheumatoid Arthritis (EIRA) study, the North American RA Consortium (NARAC) study, and the Dutch Leiden Early Arthritis Clinic study (in total, 1,977 cases and 2,405 controls)
Consistent interaction, defined as departure from additivity, between HLA-DRB1 SE alleles and the A allele of PTPN22 R620W was seen in all three studies regarding anti-CCP-positive RA.

Testing for multiplicative interactions demonstrated an interaction between the two genes only when the three studies were pooled. The linkage disequilibrium approach indicated a gene-gene interaction in EIRA and NARAC, as well as in the pooled analysis.

findings.statement: In the Swedish EIRA study, Kallberg et al. (2007) found no interaction between smoking and PTPN22 R620W. The authors described a new pattern of interactions between the 2 major known genetic risk factors (HLA-DRB1 SE and PTPN22) and the major environmental risk factor (smoking) for the risk of anti-CCP-positive RA, which extended the basis for a pathogenetic hypothesis involving genetic and environmental factors.
quotes: No interaction was seen between smoking and PTPN22 R620W.
A new pattern of interactions is described between the two major known genetic risk factors and the major environmental risk factor concerning the risk of developing anti-CCP-positive RA.

relevance_reason: Mouse model showing that DNase II deficiency causes chronic polyarthritis resembling human rheumatoid arthritis. It is mediated by TNF-alpha.

findings.statement: Kawane et al. (2006) found that Dnase2/Ifnar1 double-knockout mice (DNase II-/- IFN-IR-/-) and mice with an induced deletion of the DNase II gene developed a chronic polyarthritis resembling human rheumatoid arthritis. A set of cytokine genes was strongly activated in the affected joints. The mice's serum contained high levels of anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody, rheumatoid factor, and matrix metalloproteinase-3.
quotes: Here we show that DNase II-/-IFN-IR-/- mice and mice with an induced deletion of the DNase II gene develop a chronic polyarthritis resembling human rheumatoid arthritis.

A set of cytokine genes was strongly activated in the affected joints of these mice, and their serum contained high levels of anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody, rheumatoid factor and matrix metalloproteinase-3.

findings.statement: Kawane et al. (2006) found that early in disease, expression of the gene encoding TNF-alpha was upregulated in the bone marrow of DNase II-deficient mice. Giving the mice anti-TNF-alpha antibody prevented arthritis. The authors concluded that when macrophages cannot degrade mammalian DNA from erythroid precursors and apoptotic cells, they produce TNF-alpha. They proposed that TNF-alpha activates synovial cells to produce various cytokines, leading to chronic polyarthritis.
quotes: Early in the pathogenesis, expression of the gene encoding tumour necrosis factor (TNF)-alpha was upregulated in the bone marrow, and administration of anti-TNF-alpha antibody prevented the development of arthritis.

These results indicate that if macrophages cannot degrade mammalian DNA from erythroid precursors and apoptotic cells, they produce TNF-alpha, which activates synovial cells to produce various cytokines, leading to the development of chronic polyarthritis.

relevance_reason: Pharmacogenetic association of HLA-G 14-bp insertion/deletion polymorphism with methotrexate response in RA; relevant to clinical management/genotype-response section.

findings.statement: Rizzo et al. (2006) found that the HLA-G 14-bp deletion/insertion polymorphism was associated with methotrexate (MTX) response in RA: the -14/-14 bp genotype was increased among MTX responders compared with nonresponders (chi-square = 6.12, P = 0.02; odds ratio = 2.46, 95% CI 1.26-4.84, P = 0.009 by logistic regression). The authors proposed this polymorphism as a therapy marker in the early phases of the disease.
quotes: The analysis of the HLA-G 14-bp polymorphism in MTX-treated RA patients has confirmed an increase of the -14/-14 bp genotype in the responder group (chi=6.12, P=0.02; chi test) (odds ratio=2.46 (95% confidence interval, 1.26-4.84) P=0.009; logistic regression model).
the association between -14/-14 bp genotype and MTX clinical outcome proposes this polymorphism as a therapy marker in the early phases of the disease.

findings.statement: Rizzo et al. (2006) showed that activation of peripheral blood mononuclear cells from healthy individuals and non-MTX-treated RA patients with methotrexate induced production of soluble HLA-G, with the highest sHLA-G1 concentrations significantly associated with the HLA-G -14/-14 bp genotype. They proposed that MTX induces anti-inflammatory sHLA-G molecules that contribute to the therapeutic response.
quotes: MTX activation induces the production of sHLA-G molecules. A significant association was observed between the highest sHLA-G1 concentrations and the -14/-14 bp genotype.
Our results propose that the MTX induces the production of the anti-inflammatory sHLA-G molecules that concur with the therapy response.

relevance_reason: Genome-wide linkage scan in RA affected sib-pair families identifying new susceptibility linkage regions (2q33, 11p12) — mapping evidence for the RA entry.

findings.statement: Amos et al. (2006) did a genome-wide linkage scan with more than 5,700 informative SNP markers (Illumina IV SNP linkage panel) in 642 Caucasian families with affected sib pairs with rheumatoid arthritis, ascertained by the North American Rheumatoid Arthritis Consortium. They found new evidence of linkage at chromosomes 2q33 (lod score of 3.52) and 11p12 (lod score of 3.09).
quotes: We have completed a genome wide linkage scan using >5700 informative single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) markers (Illumina IV SNP linkage panel) in 642 Caucasian families containing affected sibling pairs with rheumatoid arthritis (RA)
The results show striking new evidence of linkage at chromosomes 2q33 and 11p12 with logarithm of odds (LOD) scores of 3.52 and 3.09, respectively.

findings.statement: Amos et al. (2006) also found a strong, broad linkage interval around the major histocompatibility complex (lod score greater than 16), regions on chromosomes 5 and 10 with lod scores above 2.5, and further evidence of linkage (lod scores 1.46 to 2.35) on chromosomes 4, 7, 12, 16, and 18. They attributed the new evidence partly to the higher information content of the SNP panel (75.6%) compared with a microsatellite panel used previously (mean 52.6%).
quotes: In addition to a strong and broad linkage interval surrounding the major histocompatibility complex (LOD>16), regions with LOD>2.5 were observed on chromosomes 5 and 10.
Additional linkage evidence (LOD scores between 1.46 and 2.35) was also observed on chromosomes 4, 7, 12, 16 and 18.
significantly increased information content of the Illumina IV SNP linkage panel (75.6%) compared with a standard microsatellite linkage panel utilized previously (mean 52.6%)

findings.statement: Amos et al. (2006) stratified sib pairs by whether or not they had elevated anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide (anti-CCP) titers. They found that the evidence for linkage on chromosomes 4, 5, 6, and 7 varied significantly between strata.
quotes: Stratified analyses according to whether or not the sibling pair members showed elevated anticyclic citrullinated peptide titers indicates significant variation in evidence for linkage among strata on chromosomes 4, 5, 6 and 7.

relevance_reason: Pathogenesis study of BLyS/APRIL in RA synovium with a human synovium-SCID mouse chimera model; no genetic variants reported.

findings.statement: Seyler et al. (2005) examined 72 rheumatoid synovial tissues representing 3 types of synovitis (ectopic germinal center (GC)-containing, T cell-B cell aggregates without GC reactions, and diffuse infiltrates). GC+ synovitis had the highest levels of APRIL, produced exclusively by CD83+ dendritic cells, whereas BLyS was present at similar levels in all tissue types and derived exclusively from CD68+ macrophages.
quotes: We examined 72 tissues representing the 3 types of synovitis for BLyS and APRIL production and for expression of APRIL/BLyS receptors.
GC+ synovitis had the highest levels of APRIL, produced exclusively by CD83+ DCs. BLyS was present in similar levels in all tissue types and derived exclusively from CD68+ macrophages.

findings.statement: Seyler et al. (2005) treated human synovium-SCID mouse chimeras with the APRIL/BLyS decoy receptor TACI:Fc. In GC+ synovitis, treatment caused GC destruction and marked inhibition of IFN-gamma and Ig transcription, whereas in aggregate and diffuse synovitis Ig levels were unaffected and IFN-gamma production was enhanced; these differential effects correlated with the presence of TACI+ T cells in aggregate and diffuse synovitis and their absence in GC+ synovitis. The authors proposed that BLyS and APRIL regulate B cell as well as T cell function and have pro- and antiinflammatory activities in RA.
quotes: In GC+ synovitis, treatment with TACI:Fc resulted in GC destruction and marked inhibition of IFN-gamma and Ig transcription. In contrast, inhibition of APRIL and BLyS in aggregate and diffuse synovitis left Ig levels unaffected and enhanced IFN-gamma production.
These differential immunomodulatory effects correlated with the presence of TACI+ T cells in aggregate and diffuse synovitis and their absence in GC+ synovitis.
We propose that BLyS and APRIL regulate B cell as well as T cell function and have pro- and antiinflammatory activities in RA.

relevance_reason: Association study of PTPN22 variants and RA susceptibility, confirming R620W association and suggesting additional independent risk variants.

findings.statement: Carlton et al. (2005) sequenced the coding regions of PTPN22 in 48 white North American patients with RA and identified 15 previously unreported SNPs, including 2 coding SNPs in the catalytic domain. They then genotyped 37 SNPs in or near PTPN22 in 475 RA patients and 475 individually matched controls, and replicated a subset in 661 patients and 1,322 matched controls; the sole haplotype carrying the W620 risk allele (R620W, rs2476601) was strongly associated with disease in both sample sets, whereas a haplotype identical at all other SNPs but carrying R620 showed no association.
quotes: we sequenced the coding regions of this gene in 48 white North American patients with RA and identified 15 previously unreported SNPs, including 2 coding SNPs in the catalytic domain

We then genotyped 37 SNPs in or near PTPN22 in 475 patients with RA and 475 individually matched controls (sample set 1) and selected a subset of markers for replication in an additional 661 patients with RA and 1,322 individually matched controls (sample set 2).

The sole haplotype found to carry the previously identified W620 risk allele was strongly associated with disease in both sample sets, whereas another haplotype, identical at all other SNPs but carrying the R620 allele, showed no association.

findings.statement: Carlton et al. (2005) found that R620W does not fully explain the association between PTPN22 and RA, since significant case-control differences persisted in both sample sets after stratification by R620W; two SNPs on a single common haplotype were associated with RA independent of R620W, suggesting that R620W and at least one additional variant in the PTPN22 gene region influence RA susceptibility.
quotes: R620W, however, does not fully explain the association between PTPN22 and RA, since significant differences between cases and controls persisted in both sample sets after the haplotype data were stratified by R620W.

Additional analyses identified two SNPs on a single common haplotype that are associated with RA independent of R620W, suggesting that R620W and at least one additional variant in the PTPN22 gene region influence RA susceptibility.

findings.statement: Carlton et al. (2005) predicted 10 common (frequency greater than 1%) PTPN22 haplotypes in white North Americans.
quotes: Analyses of these results predict 10 common (frequency >1%) PTPN22 haplotypes in white North Americans.

relevance_reason: Mouse models of RA showing that Pik3cg knockout and PI3Kgamma inhibition protect against joint inflammation; relevant for animal model/management sections.

findings.statement: Camps et al. (2005) found that Pik3cg-null mice, which lack PI3Kgamma, were largely protected in mouse models of rheumatoid arthritis, and that this protection correlated with defective neutrophil migration.
quotes: We show that Pik3cg(-/-) mice are largely protected in mouse models of rheumatoid arthritis; this protection correlates with defective neutrophil migration, further validating PI3Kgamma as a therapeutic target.

findings.statement: Camps et al. (2005) developed specific, selective, orally active small-molecule inhibitors of PI3Kgamma. Oral treatment with a PI3Kgamma inhibitor slowed the progression of joint inflammation and damage in 2 different mouse models of rheumatoid arthritis, matching the protection seen in Pik3cg-null mice. The authors proposed selective PI3Kgamma inhibitors as possible treatments for chronic inflammatory disorders such as rheumatoid arthritis.
quotes: Here we describe the identification and development of specific, selective and orally active small-molecule inhibitors of PI3Kgamma (encoded by Pik3cg).

We also describe that oral treatment with a PI3Kgamma inhibitor suppresses the progression of joint inflammation and damage in two distinct mouse models of rheumatoid arthritis, reproducing the protective effects shown by Pik3cg(-/-) mice.
Our results identify selective PI3Kgamma inhibitors as potential therapeutic molecules for the treatment of chronic inflammatory disorders such as rheumatoid arthritis.

relevance_reason: Genome-wide microsatellite association study of rheumatoid arthritis that found 47 candidate regions and confirmed HLA-DRB1; this is supporting mapping evidence.

findings.statement: Tamiya et al. (2005) carried out a whole-genome association study of rheumatoid arthritis. They used 27,039 microsatellites spaced at about 100-kb intervals and DNA pooling across three successive genomic screens of independent case-control populations, then fine-mapped candidate regions by SNP analysis. They identified 47 candidate regions. The top 7 loci withstood the most stringent statistical tests and were narrowed down to individual genes and/or SNPs on 4 chromosomes, including the previously known HLA-DRB1 gene on 6p21.3.
quotes: charting the human genome at 100 kb intervals using a collection of 27,039 microsatellites and the DNA pooling method in three successive genomic screens of independent case-control populations
A total of 47 candidate regions were identified.

The top seven loci, withstanding the most stringent statistical tests, were dissected down to individual genes and/or SNPs on four chromosomes, including the previously known 6p21.3-encoded Major Histocompatibility Complex gene, HLA-DRB1.

findings.statement: Tamiya et al. (2005) noted that rheumatoid arthritis is a destructive joint disease that affects up to 1% of the population.
quotes: rheumatoid arthritis, a destructive joint disease affecting up to 1% of the population

relevance_reason: Experimental rat study of citrullination, anti-citrullinated protein immunity and PAD4 in collagen-induced arthritis, providing pathogenesis and animal-model evidence relevant to rheumatoid arthritis; no human genetic variants reported.

findings.statement: Lundberg et al. (2005) showed in female Lew.1AV1 rats that immunisation with citrullinated rat serum albumin (Cit-RSA), but not with unmodified rat serum albumin (RSA), induced an IgG antibody response against the citrullinated protein that cross-reacted with the native protein at all time points examined (12, 24, 35 and 61 days after immunisation; n = 7 per group), indicating that citrullination of a non-immunogenic self antigen broke B cell tolerance.
quotes: Lew.1AV1 rats were immunised with the non-immunogenic autoantigen RSA or the modified counterpart Cit-RSA and the differences in induced immune responses were analysed in vitro. The kinetics of the antigen-specific IgG response was investigated and the results revealed not only a response towards the modified protein, but also cross-reactivity to the unmodified form of RSA (Fig. 4).

Antibodies were detected from 12 days after immunisation, had increased by day 24 after immunisation and persisted for a further 40 days. Cross-reactivity was demonstrated at all time points. No B cell response was noted in animals immunised with unmodified RSA.

findings.statement: Lundberg et al. (2005) found that lymph node cells taken 10 days after immunisation from Lew.1AV1 rats immunised with Cit-RSA proliferated significantly more strongly in response to Cit-RSA than did cells from RSA-immunised rats (P < 0.05), with a similar but non-significant trend on stimulation with unmodified RSA; the authors concluded that RSA with strong adjuvant can induce an autoreactive T cell response insufficient for B cell help, whereas Cit-RSA induced a stronger T cell response capable of conferring B cell help.
quotes: Cells from animals immunised with Cit-RSA showed a stronger proliferation than the RSA-immunised rats in response to the modified protein. The same tendency was observed when using RSA as a stimulus, although it was not statistically significant.

This indicates that RSA, together with a strong adjuvant, can induce an autoreactive T cell response, although this is not sufficient to induce B cell help. In contrast, immunisation with Cit-RSA induced a stronger T cell response that could confer B cell help, as depicted in Fig. 4.

findings.statement: In the rat collagen-induced arthritis model, Lundberg et al. (2005) reported that immunisation of Lew.1AV1 rats with citrullinated rat collagen type II (Cit-CII) induced arthritis with significantly higher incidence (35% higher in the early phase, 15% higher at end stage) and earlier onset (day 13 versus day 16 after immunisation) than the same amount of unmodified CII (20 animals per group), with a non-significant trend toward higher mean arthritis score; given the low arginine content of CII the authors concluded that conversion of arginine to citrulline is a highly potent mechanism for increased autoreactivity.
quotes: The citrullinated form of CII induced arthritis with significantly higher incidence and earlier onset than did the same amount of unmodified CII (Fig. 6). The incidence was 35% higher in the Cit-RSA group during the early phase of the disease and 15% higher during the end stage. Disease onset in this group occurred 13 days after immunisation, compared with 16 days after immunisation in the control group.
Considering the low arginine content of CII, our results indicate that protein modification by the conversion of arginine to citrulline is a highly potent mechanism for increased autoreactivity.

findings.statement: Using immunohistochemistry on ankle joint synovial tissue of male Dark Agouti rats with collagen-induced arthritis, Lundberg et al. (2005) demonstrated for the first time the kinetics of citrullinated proteins in arthritic joints: citrulline staining (with the RA-patient-derived recombinant antibody RA3, confirmed with anti-modified-citrulline antibodies) first appeared after disease onset at day 21 after immunisation and increased as disease became more severe and chronic (days 28 and 38), while unimmunised animals and all earlier time points including the day of onset (day 15) were negative; staining was mainly in extracellular deposits, presumably fibrin, but also in infiltrating cells and on the cartilage surface, and was joint-specific (lung, ear, spinal cord, spleen, lymph nodes and salivary glands were negative).
quotes: The first appearance of protein citrullination was noted after disease onset, at day 21 after immunisation, and increased staining was observed as the disease progressed into a more severe, chronic state (namely 28 and 38 days after immunisation). Unimmunised animals and time points before clinical signs of arthritis (namely 0, 3, 6 and 10 days after immunisation) as well as the time of disease onset (namely 15 days after immunisation) were negative for citrulline.

Some infiltrating cells as well as the cartilage surface stained positively for citrulline and the major sources of citrullinated proteins in the arthritic joint were extracellular deposits, presumably fibrin deposits. The occurrence of citrullinated proteins in the joints is specific, because other investigated organs such as lung, ear, spinal cord, spleen, lymph nodes and salivary glands were all negative (data not shown).

findings.statement: Lundberg et al. (2005) detected the citrullinating enzyme PAD4 in synovial tissue of rats with collagen-induced arthritis from 21 days after immunisation, localised to the cytoplasm of infiltrating mononuclear cells, with increasing numbers of positive cells by days 28 and 38; PAD4 was not detectable in healthy synovium or at days 3, 6, 10 or 15 after immunisation despite apparent inflammation at day 15, and its amount correlated with severity of inflammation.
quotes: PAD4, which has been reported to be present in mouse and human arthritic synovia, could also be detected in synovial tissue of this rat arthritis model from 21 days after immunisation (Fig. 3 and Table 1). The number of positive cells localised to the synovial infiltrate increased by days 28 and 38 after immunisation. PAD4 was not evident in healthy synovial tissue, nor in sections from 3, 6 and 10 days after immunisation; although an apparent inflammation was observed, PAD4 could not be detected 15 days after immunisation.
Although PAD4 has been described to have a nuclear localisation, our stainings clearly demonstrate the presence of this enzyme in the cytoplasm of infiltrating mononuclear cells.

findings.statement: From these findings Lundberg et al. (2005) concluded that citrullination can break tolerance against the ubiquitous self antigen rat serum albumin and increase the arthritogenicity of the tissue-specific protein collagen type II, and because citrullinated proteins and PAD4 were not detectable in joints before clinical arthritis they postulated that in this model citrullination is a result rather than an initiator of inflammation; they hypothesised that in individuals with the appropriate genetic background a subclinical inflammation, possibly occurring outside the joints (for example smoking-induced lung inflammation in carriers of the MHC shared epitope), induces citrullination of endogenous proteins and generation of anti-citrullinated protein antibodies that potentiate an inflammatory trigger in joints and thereby initiate RA.
quotes: In this experimental model of homologous CIA with 100% disease incidence, citrullinated proteins and PAD4 were not detectable before clinical signs of arthritis. Rather, as inflammation proceeded, increasing amounts of citrullinated proteins and PAD4 were detected specifically in the joints.
Perhaps the presence of citrullinated proteins in these arthritis models is not disease-initiating, but rather a result of inflammation.

Taking together our findings and those of others, we hypothesise that in individuals with the appropriate genetic background a subclinical inflammation that induces citrullination of endogenous proteins will generate a pathogenic immune response against the modified proteins and that through the production of autoantibodies a chronic inflammation will be established.

findings.statement: Lundberg et al. (2005) noted that an immune response towards any citrullinated protein is clearly not sufficient to induce clinical arthritis, since Cit-RSA-immunised rats, despite developing anti-citrullinated protein antibodies, showed no signs of disease, and that both genetic and environmental factors most probably contribute to arthritis development.
quotes: An immune response towards any citrullinated protein is clearly not enough to induce clinical arthritis, as demonstrated by the lack of signs of disease in the Cit-RSA-immunised animals. Both genetic and environmental factors most probably contribute to the development of arthritis.

relevance_reason: The paper reports an animal model (collagen type II-induced arthritis in DBA/1 mice) of human rheumatoid arthritis and shows that an agonistic anti-4-1BB monoclonal antibody suppresses disease, with mechanistic functional studies. This is cited as supporting evidence about immunotherapy and pathogenesis for the rheumatoid arthritis entry rather than establishing a genetic cause.

findings.statement: Seo et al. (2004) noted that collagen type II-induced arthritis, a CD4+ T-cell-dependent chronic inflammation of susceptible DBA/1 mice, represents an animal model of human rheumatoid arthritis, and found that both the development of this condition and even established disease were inhibited by an agonistic anti-4-1BB monoclonal antibody.
quotes: Collagen type II-induced arthritis is a CD4(+) T-cell-dependent chronic inflammation in susceptible DBA/1 mice and represents an animal model of human rheumatoid arthritis.
We found that development of this condition, and even established disease, are inhibited by an agonistic anti-4-1BB monoclonal antibody.

findings.statement: Seo et al. (2004) reported that anti-4-1BB antibody suppressed serum antibodies to collagen type II and CD4+ T-cell recall responses to collagen type II, and that crosslinking of 4-1BB evoked an antigen-specific, active suppression mechanism that differed from the results of blocking the interaction between 4-1BB and its ligand, 4-1BBL.
quotes: Anti-4-1BB suppressed serum antibodies to collagen type II and CD4(+) T-cell recall responses to collagen type II.
Crosslinking of 4-1BB evoked an antigen-specific, active suppression mechanism that differed from the results of blocking the interaction between 4-1BB and its ligand, 4-1BBL.

findings.statement: Seo et al. (2004) found that anti-4-1BB monoclonal antibodies induced massive, antigen-dependent clonal expansion of CD11c+CD8+ T cells and accumulation of indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase in CD11b+ monocytes and CD11c+ dendritic cells, and that both anti-interferon-gamma and 1-methyltryptophan, a pharmacological inhibitor of indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase, reversed the anti-4-1BB effect. The authors concluded that suppression of collagen-induced arthritis was caused by expansion of new CD11c+CD8+ T cells and that interferon-gamma produced by these cells suppresses antigen-specific CD4+ T cells through an indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase-dependent mechanism.
quotes: Anti-4-1BB monoclonal antibodies induced massive, antigen-dependent clonal expansion of CD11c(+)CD8(+) T cells and accumulation of indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase in CD11b(+) monocytes and CD11c(+) dendritic cells.
Both anti-interferon-gamma and 1-methyltryptophan, a pharmacological inhibitor of indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase, reversed the anti-4-1BB effect.

We conclude that the suppression of collagen-induced arthritis was caused by an expansion of new CD11c(+)CD8(+) T cells, and that interferon-gamma produced by these cells suppresses antigen-specific CD4(+) T cells through an indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase-dependent mechanism.

relevance_reason: A case-control study with a replication sample that found the minor allele of a missense SNP in PTPN22 is associated with susceptibility to rheumatoid arthritis.

findings.statement: Begovich et al. (2004) tested putative functional SNPs for association with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) in white individuals using a case-control design, then tested a second sample for replication. They found that the minor allele of a missense SNP in PTPN22, which encodes the hematopoietic-specific protein tyrosine phosphatase Lyp, was associated with RA susceptibility (discovery-study allelic P = 6.6 x 10(-4); replication-study allelic P = 5.6 x 10(-8)). The risk allele was present in about 28% of white individuals with RA and about 17% of white individuals from the general population.
quotes: Here we report the association of RA susceptibility with the minor allele of a missense SNP in PTPN22 (discovery-study allelic P=6.6 x 10(-4); replication-study allelic P=5.6 x 10(-8)), which encodes a hematopoietic-specific protein tyrosine phosphatase also known as "Lyp."
the risk allele, which is present in approximately 17% of white individuals from the general population and in approximately 28% of white individuals with RA

variants.as_reported: minor allele of a missense SNP in PTPN22

findings.statement: Begovich et al. (2004) showed that the PTPN22 risk allele disrupts the P1 proline-rich motif, which is important for interaction with Csk. They noted this could alter the normal function of these proteins as negative regulators of T-cell activation. Because the same allele had recently been implicated in type 1 diabetes, the authors suggested that the variant phosphatase may increase overall immune reactivity and raise a carrier's risk of autoimmune disease.
quotes: disrupts the P1 proline-rich motif that is important for interaction with Csk, potentially altering these proteins' normal function as negative regulators of T-cell activation

The minor allele of this SNP recently was implicated in type 1 diabetes, suggesting that the variant phosphatase may increase overall reactivity of the immune system and may heighten an individual carrier's risk for autoimmune disease.

findings.statement: Begovich et al. (2004) described rheumatoid arthritis as the most common systemic autoimmune disease, affecting about 1% of adults worldwide, with an estimated heritability of 60%.
quotes: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is the most common systemic autoimmune disease, affecting approximately 1% of the adult population worldwide, with an estimated heritability of 60%.

relevance_reason: Genome-wide SNP linkage scan in RA multiplex families that confirmed HLA-DRB1 linkage and found four more loci at nominal significance; adds mapping evidence.

findings.statement: John et al. (2004) carried out a whole-genome linkage screen of 157 families with multiple cases of rheumatoid arthritis using 11,245 genomewide SNPs and compared it with a 10-cM microsatellite scan of the same cohort. The SNP analysis detected the major RA susceptibility locus, HLA-DRB1 (P = 0.00004), with a linkage interval of 31 cM, compared with 50 cM in the microsatellite scan. Four more loci reached nominal significance (P less than 0.05) in the SNP analysis but were not seen in the microsatellite scan.
quotes: Here, we describe a whole-genome screen of 157 families with multiple cases of rheumatoid arthritis (RA), performed using 11,245 genomewide SNPs.
The SNP analysis detected HLA*DRB1, the major RA susceptibility locus (P=.00004), with a linkage interval of 31 cM, compared with a 50-cM linkage interval detected by the microsatellite scan.
In addition, four loci were detected at a nominal significance level (P<.05) in the SNP linkage analysis; these were not observed in the microsatellite scan.

findings.statement: John et al. (2004) found that differences between the SNP and microsatellite scans were mainly due to information content, which was significantly higher for the SNPs. When the SNP set was reduced to 3,300 markers (1-cM spacing), several loci fell below nominal significance. Map differences, genotyping error and moderate linkage disequilibrium between markers did not significantly affect the results.
quotes: We demonstrate that variation in information content was the main factor contributing to observed differences in the two scans, with the SNPs providing significantly higher information content than the microsatellites.
Reducing the number of SNPs in the marker set to 3,300 (1-cM spacing) caused several loci to drop below nominal significance levels

relevance_reason: The paper describes a mouse model in which a spontaneous Zap70 SH2-domain point mutation causes autoimmune arthritis resembling human RA. It also proposes a thymic-selection mechanism that may apply to some patients with RA.

findings.statement: Sakaguchi et al. (2003) found that in mice, a spontaneous point mutation in the gene region encoding an SH2 domain of ZAP-70, a key T-cell signal transduction molecule, caused chronic autoimmune arthritis that resembled human rheumatoid arthritis in many respects.
quotes: Here we show that a spontaneous point mutation of the gene encoding an SH2 domain of ZAP-70, a key signal transduction molecule in T cells, causes chronic autoimmune arthritis in mice that resembles human RA in many aspects.

variants.as_reported: spontaneous point mutation of the gene encoding an SH2 domain of ZAP-70

findings.statement: Sakaguchi et al. (2003) reported that altered T-cell receptor signaling through the aberrant ZAP-70 changed the thresholds of T cells to thymic selection. As a result, autoimmune T cells that would otherwise be negatively selected were positively selected. They suggested that thymic production of arthritogenic T cells, caused by a genetically determined shift of the T-cell repertoire toward high self-reactivity, might also be crucial to disease development in a subset of patients with RA.
quotes: Altered signal transduction from T-cell antigen receptor through the aberrant ZAP-70 changes the thresholds of T cells to thymic selection, leading to the positive selection of otherwise negatively selected autoimmune T cells.

Thymic production of arthritogenic T cells due to a genetically determined selection shift of the T-cell repertoire towards high self-reactivity might also be crucial to the development of disease in a subset of patients with RA.

relevance_reason: Case-control LD mapping found that SLC22A4 and RUNX1 SNPs are associated with susceptibility to rheumatoid arthritis in Japanese people, and functional work showed how RUNX1 regulates SLC22A4.

findings.statement: Tokuhiro et al. (2003) used SNPs in a case-control linkage disequilibrium mapping study of the cytokine gene cluster on chromosome 5q31 in the Japanese population. They found a significant association between rheumatoid arthritis and the organic cation transporter gene SLC22A4 (P = 0.000034).
quotes: We investigated the genetic contribution of the cytokine gene cluster in chromosome 5q31 to susceptibility to rheumatoid arthritis in the Japanese population by case-control linkage disequilibrium (LD) mapping using single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs).
Here we report that there is significant association between rheumatoid arthritis and the organic cation transporter gene SLC22A4 (P = 0.000034).

findings.statement: Tokuhiro et al. (2003) found that an intronic SNP in SLC22A4, associated with rheumatoid arthritis, lies in a RUNX1 binding site. In vitro, this SNP affected the transcriptional efficiency of SLC22A4 because the two alleles differed in their affinity for the hematopoietic transcriptional regulator RUNX1.
quotes: A SNP affects the transcriptional efficiency of SLC22A4 in vitro, owing to an allelic difference in affinity to Runt-related transcription factor 1 (RUNX1), a transcriptional regulator in the hematopoietic system.

variants.as_reported: intronic SNP in a RUNX1 binding site of SLC22A4

findings.statement: Tokuhiro et al. (2003) found that a SNP in RUNX1 was also strongly associated with rheumatoid arthritis (P = 0.00035). They concluded that RUNX1 regulation of SLC22A4 expression is associated with susceptibility to rheumatoid arthritis and suggested this may be an example of an epistatic effect of two genes on the disorder.
quotes: A SNP in RUNX1 is also strongly associated with rheumatoid arthritis (P = 0.00035).

Our data indicate that the regulation of SLC22A4 expression by RUNX1 is associated with susceptibility to rheumatoid arthritis, which may represent an example of an epistatic effect of two genes on this disorder.

findings.statement: Tokuhiro et al. (2003) showed that SLC22A4 expression is specific to hematological and immunological tissues. SLC22A4 was also highly expressed in the inflamed joints of mice with collagen-induced arthritis.
quotes: We show that expression of SLC22A4 is specific to hematological and immunological tissues and that SLC22A4 is also highly expressed in the inflammatory joints of mice with collagen-induced arthritis.

relevance_reason: Links HLA-DRB1*04, the main RA susceptibility allele, to early telomere loss in T cells and granulocytes. This suggests a mechanism for the T-cell senescence seen in RA.

findings.statement: Schönland et al. (2003) studied whether HLA-DRB1*04 alleles, the major susceptibility genes for rheumatoid arthritis, confer risk for T-cell senescence. In healthy individuals, HLA-DRB1*04 alleles were associated with excessive loss of telomeres in CD4+ T cells. This accelerated erosion occurred during the first 2 decades of life and was followed by reduced homeostatic T-cell proliferation in adulthood. Telomeric repair mechanisms were intact in HLA-DRB1*04+ donors.
quotes: In healthy individuals, HLA-DRB1*04 alleles were associated with excessive loss of telomeres in CD4+ T cells.
Accelerated telomeric erosion occurred during the first two decades of life and was followed by reduced homeostatic T cell proliferation during adulthood.
Telomeric repair mechanisms were intact in HLA-DRB1*04+ donors.

findings.statement: Schönland et al. (2003) found that premature telomeric loss also affected granulocytes, which suggested that the hematopoietic stem cell is the primary target. They proposed that HLA-DRB1*04 alleles, or genes in linkage disequilibrium with them, regulate stem cell replication and contribute to the accumulation of senescent and autoreactive T cells in rheumatoid arthritis.
quotes: Premature telomeric loss also affected granulocytes, suggesting that the hematopoietic stem cell is the primary target.
We propose that HLA-DRB1*04 alleles or genes in linkage disequilibrium regulate stem cell replication and contribute to the accumulation of senescent and autoreactive T cells in rheumatoid arthritis.

relevance_reason: Association study linking IFNG/IL26 region microsatellite markers on 12q15 to sex-specific susceptibility to RA.

findings.statement: Vandenbroeck et al. (2003) genotyped 4 microsatellite markers in a 118-kb interval containing the IFNG and IL26 genes on chromosome 12q15 in 251 patients with RA and 198 unrelated healthy controls from Northern Ireland. Marker D12S2510, located 3 kb 3-prime of IL26, was significantly associated with RA in women (corrected P = 0.008) but not in men (P = 0.99). A 3-marker haplotype, IFNGCA*13;D12S2510*8;D12S2511*9, was significantly underrepresented in women with RA (odds ratio 0.50; corrected P = 0.03) but not in men. The authors concluded that common polymorphisms in the IFNG/IL26 region may contribute to sex bias in RA susceptibility.
quotes: Four microsatellite markers, located in a 118-kb interval that contains both the IFNgamma and IL-26 genes on chromosome 12q15, were typed in 251 patients with RA and 198 unrelated healthy controls (all of whom lived in Northern Ireland)

Marker D12S2510, which is located 3 kb 3' from the IL-26 gene, was significantly associated with RA in women (corrected P [P(corr)] = 0.008, 2 degrees of freedom [2 df]) but not in men (P = 0.99, 2 df).

A 3-marker haplotype, IFNGCA*13;D12S2510*8;D12S2511*9, was inferred that showed significant underrepresentation in women with RA (odds ratio 0.50, 95% confidence interval 0.32-0.78; P = 0.002, P(corr) = 0.03) but not in men with RA.

relevance_reason: The title shows a family and genetic study of rheumatoid arthritis and rheumatoid factor in Blackfeet Indians, which bears on familial aggregation and inheritance of RA. Only the title was available, so no results can be extracted.

findings.statement: BURCH et al. (1964) reported family and genetic studies of rheumatoid arthritis and rheumatoid factor in Blackfeet Indians.
quotes: FAMILY AND GENETIC STUDIES OF RHEUMATOID ARTHRITIS AND RHEUMATOID FACTOR IN BLACKFEET INDIANS.

relevance_reason: Only the title is available. It shows the paper studied familial factors in rheumatoid arthritis, which bears on the inheritance of RA, but it gives no data.

findings.statement: GOWANS et al. (1964) studied familial factors in rheumatoid arthritis.
quotes: FAMILIAL FACTORS IN RHEUMATOID ARTHRITIS.

relevance_reason: Association study of an IL10 promoter polymorphism with RA severity (joint destruction) and autoantibody production; no association with RA susceptibility.

findings.statement: Lard et al. (2003) genotyped the -2849 A/G IL10 promoter polymorphism, which is associated with high (AG/GG) and low (AA) IL-10 production, in 283 RA patients, 413 patients with other rheumatic diseases, and 1,220 healthy controls. The IL10 genotype was not associated with the incidence of RA, but was associated with disease progression: patients with the high-IL-10-production genotype had a higher rate of joint destruction and higher baseline autoantibody titers (IgG and IgM rheumatoid factors and anti-citrullinated peptide antibodies).
quotes: Allele frequencies of the promoter polymorphism -2849 A/G and carriage rates were compared in 283 RA patients, 413 patients with other rheumatic diseases, and 1,220 healthy controls.

The IL-10 genotype was not associated with the incidence of RA, but instead, correlated with disease progression, as determined by the extent of joint destruction. A higher rate of joint destruction was observed in patients with the genotype associated with high IL-10 production.
Instead, patients with the -2849 AG/GG genotype, which is associated with high IL-10 production, had higher autoantibody titers at baseline.

findings.statement: Lard et al. (2003) found that adenoviral gene transfer of IL10 to fibroblast-like synoviocytes (FLS) inhibited their invasiveness, but FLS invasiveness in vitro did not differ between RA patients who were -2849 G carriers and non-G carriers. They concluded that the -2849 IL10 promoter polymorphism is associated with autoantibody production and subsequent joint damage in RA.
quotes: Although adenoviral gene transfer of IL-10 to FLS inhibited their invasiveness, no differences were observed in vitro in the FLS from RA patients who were -2849 non-G carriers compared with those who were G carriers.
The -2849 IL-10 promoter polymorphism is associated with autoantibody production and subsequent joint damage in RA.

relevance_reason: Functional and transgenic-mouse study addressing how the RA-associated HLA-DRB1*0401 shared epitope binds citrullinated peptides and activates CD4+ T cells, providing mechanistic evidence relevant to RA pathogenesis.

findings.statement: Hill et al. (2003) noted that rheumatoid arthritis is genetically associated with MHC class II molecules containing the shared epitope, and postulated that these MHC molecules may participate in disease pathogenesis by selectively binding arthritogenic peptides for presentation to autoreactive CD4+ T cells; they noted that posttranslationally modified proteins containing citrulline (deiminated arginine) had recently been identified as specific targets of the IgG antibody response in RA patients.
quotes: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is genetically associated with MHC class II molecules that contain the shared epitope. These MHC molecules may participate in disease pathogenesis by selectively binding arthritogenic peptides for presentation to autoreactive CD4(+) T cells.
recent work has identified posttranslationally modified proteins containing citrulline (deiminated arginine) as specific targets of the IgG Ab response in RA patients

findings.statement: To understand how citrulline might evoke an autoimmune reaction, Hill et al. (2003) studied T cell responses to citrulline-containing peptides in HLA-DRB1*0401 transgenic (DR4-IE tg) mice and demonstrated that conversion of arginine to citrulline at the peptide side-chain position interacting with the shared epitope significantly increased peptide-MHC affinity and led to activation of CD4+ T cells in these mice.
quotes: To understand how citrulline might evoke an autoimmune reaction, we have studied T cell responses to citrulline-containing peptides in HLA-DRB1*0401 transgenic (DR4-IE tg) mice.

In this study, we demonstrate that the conversion of arginine to citrulline at the peptide side-chain position interacting with the shared epitope significantly increases peptide-MHC affinity and leads to the activation CD4(+) T cells in DR4-IE tg mice.

findings.statement: Hill et al. (2003) concluded that their results revealed how DRB1 alleles carrying the shared epitope could initiate an autoimmune response to citrullinated self-antigens in patients with rheumatoid arthritis.
quotes: These results reveal how DRB1 alleles with the shared epitope could initiate an autoimmune response to citrullinated self-Ags in RA patients.

relevance_reason: Identifies PADI4 as a susceptibility locus for rheumatoid arthritis through a case-control association study, and shows the risk haplotype affects transcript stability and anti-citrullinated peptide antibody levels.

findings.statement: Suzuki et al. (2003) used a case-control linkage disequilibrium study to show that PADI4, one of 4 PADI genes in a previously linked RA susceptibility region, is a susceptibility locus for rheumatoid arthritis (P = 0.000008). They identified a PADI4 haplotype associated with RA susceptibility.
quotes: We used a case-control linkage disequilibrium study to show that PADI type 4 is a susceptibility locus for rheumatoid arthritis (P = 0.000008).
Previous linkage studies have shown that a susceptibility locus for rheumatoid arthritis includes four PADI genes but did not establish which PADI gene confers susceptibility to rheumatoid arthritis.

findings.statement: Suzuki et al. (2003) found that the RA-susceptibility PADI4 haplotype affected transcript stability and was associated with levels of antibody to citrullinated peptide in sera from patients with RA. PADI4 was expressed in hematologic tissues and RA synovial tissues. The authors suggested that the susceptibility haplotype increases production of citrullinated peptides that act as autoantigens, heightening risk of disease.
quotes: We also identified a haplotype of PADI4 associated with susceptibility to rheumatoid arthritis that affected stability of transcripts and was associated with levels of antibody to citrullinated peptide in sera from individuals with rheumatoid arthritis.
PADI4 was expressed in hematological and rheumatoid arthritis synovial tissues.

Our results imply that the PADI4 haplotype associated with susceptibility to rheumatoid arthritis increases production of citrullinated peptides acting as autoantigens, resulting in heightened risk of developing the disease.

relevance_reason: Meta-analysis of genome-wide linkage studies identifying RA susceptibility loci, including chromosome 16, for the mapping section.

findings.statement: Fisher et al. (2003) carried out a genome-search meta-analysis of the published results of 4 genome-wide linkage studies of rheumatoid arthritis. They defined 120 genomic bins of about 30 cM each and ranked them by maximum evidence for linkage. Apart from the HLA locus (P < 0.00002), the strongest evidence for an RA susceptibility locus was on chromosome 16 (P = 0.004). None of the 4 individual genome searches had found this locus to be statistically significant.
quotes: In addition to the HLA locus (P < 0.00002), the strongest evidence for an RA susceptibility locus was found on chromosome 16 (P = 0.004). This locus was not identified as statistically significant in any of the 4 individual RA genome searches.
For each study, 120 genomic bins of approximately 30 cM were defined and ranked according to the maximum evidence for linkage within each bin.

findings.statement: In the meta-analysis by Fisher et al. (2003), 12 regions reached a significant summed rank (P < 0.05), whereas 6 bins would be expected by chance. Four of these regions, on 6p, 16cen, 6q, and 12p, reached P < 0.01. The authors suggested that a subset of these regions contains RA susceptibility loci.
quotes: In total, 12 regions achieved a significant (P < 0.05) summed rank, compared with the 6 bins expected by random chance. Four of these regions (on chromosomes 6p, 16cen, 6q, and 12p) reached a significance value of P < 0.01, suggesting that a subset of these regions contains RA susceptibility loci.

relevance_reason: Reports a CD44 splice variant (CD44vRA) in RA synovial fluid cells and functional studies suggesting a pathogenic mechanism; does not establish germline causation.

findings.statement: Nedvetzki et al. (2003) found that synovial fluid cells from the joints of patients with rheumatoid arthritis expressed a novel CD44 variant, designated CD44vRA, which carried an extra CAG trinucleotide transcribed from intronic sequences flanking a variant exon. CD44vRA was detected in 23 of 30 RA patients.
quotes: Synovial fluid cells from joints of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) patients express a novel variant of CD44 (designated CD44vRA), encoding an extra trinucleotide (CAG) transcribed from intronic sequences flanking a variant exon.
The CD44vRA mutant was detected in 23 out of 30 RA patients.

findings.statement: Nedvetzki et al. (2003) showed that CD44-negative Namalwa cells transfected with CD44vRA or wildtype CD44v3-v10 bound FGF2 equally through heparan sulfate chains, but cells immobilizing FGF2 via CD44vRA bound substantially more soluble FGFR1 and stimulated proliferation of FGFR1-bearing BaF-32 cells more efficiently. Primary RA synovial fluid cells expressing CD44vRA bound more soluble FGFR1 than synovial cells expressing CD44v3-v10 or osteoarthritis synovial cells, and this binding was reduced by antibodies against the CD44 v3 exon product. The authors suggested that this enhanced FGF2–FGFR1 interaction may foster the destructive inflammatory cascade in RA and possibly other autoimmune diseases.
quotes: Namalwa cells, immobilizing FGF-2 via their cell surface CD44vRA, bound substantially more soluble FGF receptor-1 (FGFR-1) than did Namalwa cells immobilizing the same amount of FGF-2 via their cell surface CD44v3-v10.

isolated primary synovial fluid cells from RA patients expressing CD44vRA bound more soluble FGFR-1 to their cell surface-associated FGF-2 than did corresponding synovial cells expressing CD44v3-v10 or synovial cells from osteoarthritis patients.
A similar mechanism may foster the destructive inflammatory cascade not only in RA, but also in other autoimmune diseases.

relevance_reason: Association study that identifies a second RA susceptibility locus in the MHC: a promoter SNP in the IkappaBL (NFKBIL1) gene in Japanese patients.

findings.statement: In Japanese patients with RA and a control group, Okamoto et al. (2003) had earlier reported a second RA susceptibility gene in the telomeric HLA class III region, apart from HLA-DRB1. Using microsatellites, they narrowed the region to 70 kb telomeric of the TNF cluster, which contains 4 expressed genes (IkappaBL, ATP6G, BAT1, and MICB).
quotes: in a set of Japanese patients with RA and a control group, we previously reported the presence of a second RA-susceptibility gene within the telomeric human leukocyte antigen (HLA) class III region
Using microsatellites, we narrowed the susceptibility region to 70 kb telomeric of the TNF cluster, known to harbor four expressed genes (I kappa BL, ATP6G, BAT1, and MICB).

findings.statement: Using many SNPs and insertion/deletion polymorphisms, Okamoto et al. (2003) identified the second RA susceptibility locus in the HLA region as the T allele of SNP 96452 (T/A), at position -62 in the promoter of the IkappaBL gene (P = 0.0062), in Japanese patients. The -62T/A SNP disrupts a putative binding motif for the transcriptional repressor deltaEF1, so it may affect IkappaBL transcription. IkappaBL is homologous to IkappaB-alpha, a known inhibitor of NF-kappa-B.
quotes: we identify the second RA-susceptibility locus within the HLA region, as the T allele of SNP 96452 (T/A), in the promoter region (position -62) of the I kappa BL gene (P=.0062)
This -62T/A SNP disrupts the putative binding motif for the transcriptional repressor, delta EF1, and hence may influence the transcription of I kappa BL

findings.statement: Okamoto et al. (2003) suggested that the MHC may contain RA genetic determinants that affect both the innate immune system (through IkappaBL and NF-kappa-B) and the adaptive immune system (through HLA-DRB1).
quotes: Therefore, the MHC may harbor RA genetic determinants affecting the innate and adaptive arms of the immune system.

relevance_reason: Haplotype association analysis of the HLA complex in 469 multicase RA families, identifying MHC risk effects beyond HLA-DRB1.

findings.statement: Jawaheer et al. (2002) performed extensive haplotype analysis using 54 markers distributed across the entire HLA complex in 469 multicase families with RA. They found that, in addition to associations with HLA-DRB1 alleles, at least 2 additional genetic effects were present within the MHC. One lay within a 497-kb region in the central portion of the HLA complex, an interval that excludes DRB1, on a segment of the highly conserved ancestral A1-B8-DRB1*03 (8.1) haplotype.
quotes: We have performed an extensive haplotype analysis, using 54 markers distributed across the entire HLA complex, in a set of 469 multicase families with RA.

in addition to associations with the DRB1 alleles, at least two additional genetic effects are present within the major histocompatibility complex. One of these lies within a 497-kb region in the central portion of the HLA complex, an interval that excludes DRB1.
This genetic risk factor is present on a segment of a highly conserved ancestral A1-B8-DRB1*03 (8.1) haplotype.

findings.statement: Jawaheer et al. (2002) suggested that additional risk genes may also be present in the HLA class I region in a subset of DRB1*0404 haplotypes, and concluded that HLA associations with RA are complex and cannot be completely explained by the DRB1 locus.
quotes: Additional risk genes may also be present in the HLA class I region in a subset of DRB1*0404 haplotypes.
they clearly demonstrate that such associations with RA are complex and cannot be completely explained by the DRB1 locus.

relevance_reason: Functional/mechanistic study of rheumatoid factor B-cell activation via BCR and TLR9 dual engagement; relevant to RA pathogenesis.

findings.statement: Leadbetter et al. (2002) showed that effective activation of B cells expressing rheumatoid factor (RF), an antigen receptor specific for self-IgG, was mediated by IgG2a-chromatin immune complexes and required synergistic engagement of the antigen receptor and a member of the MyD88-dependent Toll-like receptor family; inhibitor studies implicated TLR9. The authors concluded that these data established a critical link between innate and adaptive immunity in the development of systemic autoimmune disease and explained the preponderance of autoantibodies reactive with nucleic acid-protein particles.
quotes: Here we show that effective activation of RF+ B cells is mediated by IgG2a-chromatin immune complexes and requires the synergistic engagement of the antigen receptor and a member of the MyD88-dependent Toll-like receptor (TLR) family. Inhibitor studies implicate TLR9.

These data establish a critical link between the innate and adaptive immune systems in the development of systemic autoimmune disease and explain the preponderance of autoantibodies reactive with nucleic acid-protein particles.

relevance_reason: Reports linkage and association mapping of a novel RA susceptibility locus on 17q22, which belongs in the mapping section of the RA entry.

findings.statement: Barton et al. (2001) studied linkage in rheumatoid arthritis affected sib-pair (ASP) families to 5 human regions homologous to loci found in animal models of inflammatory arthritis. They found linkage to 17q22 in 200 RA ASP families and replicated it in another 100 ASP families. This region is syntenic to a susceptibility locus shared by 2 experimental rat models. Typing additional markers narrowed the linked region to 4 cM.
quotes: We have investigated linkage to five regions homologous to those identified in animal models of inflammatory arthritis in RA affected sibling pair (ASP) families.
Linkage to 17q22 syntenic to a susceptibility locus common to two experimental rat models was detected in 200 RA ASP families and replicated in a further 100 RA ASP families.
Linkage to additional markers mapping to the area has refined the extent of linkage to a 4 cM region.

findings.statement: Barton et al. (2001) found association between rheumatoid arthritis and marker D17S807 on 17q22 in their ASP cohort, using extensions of the transmission disequilibrium test. In an independent cohort of families with a single RA case, 2 two-marker haplotypes that included D17S807 were associated with RA. This narrowed the region likely to contain the causative mutation to about 1 cM.
quotes: Association to one of the markers (D17S807) was demonstrated in this cohort using extensions of the transmission disequilibrium test.

Association to two 2-marker haplotypes including this marker was detected in an independent cohort of single-case RA families, thus narrowing the region harbouring the aetiological mutation to approximately 1 cM.

findings.statement: Barton et al. (2001) described rheumatoid arthritis as an oligogenic autoimmune disease. They noted that the only consistent genetic finding had been linkage and association to the MHC, which is estimated to account for only 30 to 40% of the total genetic component of susceptibility.
quotes: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is an oligogenic autoimmune disease but, to date, linkage and association to major histocompatibility complex (MHC) has been the only consistent finding in genetic studies.
However, MHC is estimated to contribute only 30-40% of the total genetic component to disease susceptibility.

relevance_reason: Reports anti-GPI autoantibodies and elevated soluble GPI in RA patients, linking the K/BxN mouse model to human RA pathogenesis.

findings.statement: Schaller et al. (2001) found that 64% of patients with RA, but not controls, had increased concentrations of anti-glucose-6-phosphate isomerase (GPI) IgG in serum and synovial fluid. Concentrations of soluble GPI in the sera and synovial fluids of RA patients were also elevated, which led to immune complex formation.
quotes: Here we show that 64% of humans with RA, but not controls, had increased concentrations of anti-GPI immunoglobulin G (IgG) in serum and synovial fluid.
the concentrations of soluble GPI in the sera and synovial fluids of RA patients were also elevated, which led to immune complex formation.

phenotypes.text: anti-GPI IgG autoantibodies in serum and synovial fluid

findings.statement: Schaller et al. (2001) cloned, by phage display, a panel of specific high-affinity human monoclonal anti-GPI IgGs from a patient with RA; the antibodies were highly somatically mutated, indicating an affinity-matured, antigen-driven response. Immunohistochemistry of RA synovium showed high concentrations of GPI on the surface of the synovial lining and on the endothelial surface of arterioles, suggesting a mechanism by which anti-GPI antibodies may precipitate joint disease. The authors concluded that the immunologic events leading to arthritis in the K/BxN mouse model may also occur in human RA.
quotes: Using phage-display methods, we cloned a panel of specific high-affinity human monoclonal anti-GPI IgGs from a patient with RA. These antibodies were highly somatically mutated, which was indicative of an affinity-matured response that was antigen driven.

Immunohistochemistry of RA synovium showed high concentrations of GPI on the surface of the synovial lining and on the endothelial cell surface of arterioles; this indicated a mechanism by which antibodies to GPI may precipitate joint disease.
The results indicate that the immunological events that lead to the development of autoimmune disease in the K/BxN mouse model may also occur in human RA.

relevance_reason: Association study identifying KIR2DS2 and HLA-C alleles as genetic risk modifiers for rheumatoid vasculitis, an extraarticular complication of RA; also functional data on KIR2DS2 on CD4+CD28null T cells.

findings.statement: Yen et al. (2001) genotyped KIR2DS1 and KIR2DS2 in 76 healthy controls, 70 RA patients without major organ involvement, and 30 RA patients with rheumatoid vasculitis, all Caucasians of Western European descent. KIR2DS2 was present in 83% of patients with rheumatoid vasculitis versus 47% of controls (odds ratio 5.56, P = 0.001) and 39% of patients with uncomplicated RA (odds ratio 7.96, P = 0.001), whereas KIR2DS1 was not associated; the authors concluded that KIR2DS2 did not affect the risk of developing RA but was strongly associated with vascular complications.
quotes: The KIR2DS2 gene was significantly enriched among patients with rheumatoid vasculitis compared with normal individuals (odds ratio 5.56, P = 0.001) and patients with RA but no vasculitis (odds ratio 7.96, P = 0.001).
These data indicated that KIR2DS2 did not affect the risk of an individual to develop RA but was strongly associated with the likelihood of vascular complications.
However, KIR2DS2 was found in 83% of the cohort with rheumatoid vasculitis.

findings.statement: Yen et al. (2001) found that, compared with ethnically matched controls, RA patients had a decreased frequency of HLA-C*04 (OR 0.39) and an increased frequency of HLA-C*05 (OR 2.92). In patients with rheumatoid vasculitis, HLA-C*05 was further increased (OR 5.71, P = 0.001), and HLA-C*03 was enriched exclusively in vasculitis patients (60% positive; OR 3.74, P = 0.003). In logistic regression, HLA-C*03 (OR 8.6) and KIR2DS2 (OR 3.69) each conferred independent risk for vasculitis, with no significant interaction detected.
quotes: The decreased frequency of HLA-C*04 among patients with RA yielded an odds ratio of 0.39 (P = 0.024), and the enrichment of HLA-C*05 gave an odds ratio of 2.92 (P = 0.024; Table).
The representation of HLA-C*03 was almost doubled, with 60% of patients (corresponding to an allele frequency of 33%) typing positive (odds ratio 3.74, P = 0.003).

each demonstrated an independent significant risk associated with vasculitis (odds ratio for HLA-C*03 = 8.6, P < 0.001; odds ratio for KIR2DS2 = 3.69, P = 0.01), suggesting that both contribute a risk to vasculitis, independent of each other.

findings.statement: Yen et al. (2001) found that CD4+CD28null T-cell clones from 3 patients with rheumatoid vasculitis expressed KIR2DS2 in 58 to 91% of clones, often unopposed by the inhibitory receptors KIR2DL2/KIR2DL3, whereas such clones were rare in healthy controls. Cross-linking of CD158b on KIR2DS2+ clones enhanced IFN-gamma transcription and proliferation in response to suboptimal anti-CD3, and the authors suggested that KIR2DS2 with the appropriate HLA-C ligand may have a role in vascular damage by regulating CD4+CD28null T cells.
quotes: Of the activating receptors, expression of KIR2DS2 was prominent and ranged from 58–91% of the clones in the three patients studied.
These data demonstrate that in patients with rheumatoid vasculitis, KIR2DS2 was frequently unopposed by inhibitory receptors of related specificities on CD4+CD28null T cells.
If CD158b is cross-linked in the presence of suboptimal doses of anti-CD3, transcription of IFN-γ is upregulated from 6,628 copies to 63,300 copies.

relevance_reason: Genomewide linkage screen in RA multiplex families identifying HLA and non-HLA susceptibility loci; mapping evidence for the RA entry.

findings.statement: Jawaheer et al. (2001) performed a genomewide screen for allele sharing using 379 microsatellite markers in 257 multiplex RA families from the United States, collected by the North American Rheumatoid Arthritis Consortium, that contained 301 affected sib pairs. Nonparametric analysis with SIBPAL confirmed linkage of RA to the HLA locus (P less than 0.00005), with lambda-HLA = 1.79.
quotes: The North American Rheumatoid Arthritis Consortium, using well-defined clinical criteria, has collected 257 families containing 301 affected sibling pairs with RA. A genome screen for allele sharing was performed, using 379 microsatellite markers.
A nonparametric analysis using SIBPAL confirmed linkage of the HLA locus to RA (P < .00005), with lambdaHLA = 1.79.

findings.statement: In the same genome screen, Jawaheer et al. (2001) found evidence for linkage at P less than 0.005 to several non-HLA loci, on chromosomes 1 (D1S235), 4 (D4S1647), 12 (D12S373), 16 (D16S403), and 17 (D17S1301). MLOD analysis of X-linked markers with ASPEX also suggested linkage to the telomeric marker DXS6807. Stratifying the families into white or seropositive subgroups revealed some additional markers whose significance improved over the full data set.
quotes: However, the analysis also revealed a number of non-HLA loci on chromosomes 1 (D1S235), 4 (D4S1647), 12 (D12S373), 16 (D16S403), and 17 (D17S1301), with evidence for linkage at a significance level of P<.005.
Analysis of X-linked markers using the MLOD method from ASPEX also suggests linkage to the telomeric marker DXS6807.
Stratifying the families into white or seropositive subgroups revealed some additional markers that showed improvement in significance over the full data set.

findings.statement: Jawaheer et al. (2001) noted that several regions reaching nominal significance (P less than 0.05) had been implicated earlier in RA (D16S516 and D17S1301) or in other autoimmune diseases. These included systemic lupus erythematosus (D1S235), inflammatory bowel disease (D4S1647, D5S1462, and D16S516), multiple sclerosis (D12S1052), and ankylosing spondylitis (D16S516). The authors concluded that HLA genes play a major role in RA susceptibility but that several other regions also contribute significantly to overall genetic risk, suggesting genetic overlap with other autoimmune diseases.
quotes: Several of the regions that showed evidence for nominal significance (P < .05) in our data set had previously been implicated in RA (D16S516 and D17S1301) or in other diseases of an autoimmune nature, including systemic lupus erythematosus (D1S235), inflammatory bowel disease (D4S1647, D5S1462, and D16S516), multiple sclerosis (D12S1052), and ankylosing spondylitis (D16S516).
Therefore, genes in the HLA complex play a major role in RA susceptibility, but several other regions also contribute significantly to overall genetic risk.

relevance_reason: The paper does not report human patients or variants; it describes a rat congenic model of experimental arthritis (Oia3 on rat chromosome 10) with features likened to human rheumatoid arthritis (female preponderance), which a curator would cite as an animal model in the RA entry.

findings.statement: Holm et al.
