(2001) produced a rat strain congenic for Oia3, a quantitative trait locus originally identified as an oil-induced arthritis (OIA) QTL in arthritis-prone DA rats, by transferring a 46-cM telomeric region of chromosome 10 encompassing Oia3 from DA rats into MHC-identical but minimally arthritis-susceptible LEW.1AV1 rats by selective breeding; they noted that, although several QTLs regulating risk of experimental arthritis had been identified by genome-wide linkage analyses, only the MHC had thus far been reported to transfer arthritis susceptibility in congenic animals.
quotes: Several quantitative trait loci (QTLs) regulating the risk of experimental arthritis have been identified by genome-wide linkage analyses, but only the MHC has thus far been reported to transfer arthritis susceptibility in congenic animals.

We have produced a congenic strain for Oia3, a genetic factor originally identified as an oil-induced arthritis (OIA) QTL in arthritis-prone DA rats. A 46 cM telomeric region of chromosome 10 encompassing Oia3 was transferred from DA rats to MHC-identical but minutely arthritis-susceptible LEW.1AV1 rats by selective breeding.

findings.statement: Holm et al. (2001) provoked arthritis in Oia3-congenic rats by intradermal injection of different adjuvant oils; squalene, an endogenous cholesterol precursor that is approved for vaccinations in humans and has been implicated in Gulf War syndrome, induced T cell infiltration into joints and macroscopic arthritis in Oia3-congenic and DA rats, whereas LEW.1AV1 rats were almost resistant. Arthritis onset approximately 14 days post-injection coincided with arrested body-weight gain and increased plasma levels of the inflammation markers fibrinogen and alpha-1-acid glycoprotein, and congenic rats showed intermediate phenotypes compared with the 2 parental strains.
quotes: Arthritis development was provoked in Oia3-congenic rats by intradermal injection of different adjuvant oils. One successful arthritis trigger was squalene, which is approved for vaccinations in humans and has been implicated in Gulf War syndrome.
The endogenous cholesterol precursor squalene induced T cell infiltration into joints and macroscopic arthritis in Oia3-congenic rats and DA rats, whereas LEW.1AV1 rats were almost resistant.

Arthritis onset, approximately 14 days post-injection, coincided with arrested body-weight gain and increased plasma levels of the inflammation markers fibrinogen and alpha 1-acid glycoprotein. Congenic rats displayed intermediate phenotypes compared with the two parental strains

findings.statement: Holm et al. (2001) observed a female preponderance of squalene-induced arthritis in Oia3-congenic rats, similar to rheumatoid arthritis in humans, and by constructing recombinant rat strains mapped a susceptibility gene or genes in females to a telomeric 4-19 cM subregion of Oia3; they concluded that the experimental system allowed transformation of multifactorial arthritis susceptibility into dichotomous phenotypes.
quotes: similar to rheumatoid arthritis in humans, female preponderance was observed in Oia3-congenic rats

Finally, recombinant rat strains were constructed and were used to map a susceptibility gene(s) in females to a telomeric 4--19 cM Oia3 subregion. The experimental system described allows transformation of multifactorial arthritis susceptibility into dichotomous phenotypes.

relevance_reason: Only the title is available. It describes haplotypic SNPs in the central MHC gene IKBL, a possible regulator of NF-kappaB. The title does not mention rheumatoid arthritis, patients or disease association, so the paper gives only context for MHC candidate genes.

findings.statement: Allcock et al. (2001) described haplotypic single nucleotide polymorphisms in IKBL, a gene in the central MHC and a potential regulator of NF-kappaB function.
quotes: Haplotypic single nucleotide polymorphisms in the central MHC gene IKBL, a potential regulator of NF-kappaB function.

relevance_reason: Association mapping of a second RA susceptibility locus within the HLA class III region, telomeric of TNF.

findings.statement: Ota et al. (2001) tested 18 microsatellite markers spanning the 3.6-Mb HLA region, from HSET at the centromeric end to P5-15 at the telomeric end, for association with rheumatoid arthritis. Allele association analysis placed one RA susceptibility gene at HLA-DRB1, as expected. It also suggested a second susceptibility gene in the HLA class III region, within a 70-kb interval just telomeric of the TNF gene cluster (TNFA and LTA), between the microsatellites TNFa and C1-2-A.
quotes: Statistical studies of associated alleles on each microsatellite locus showed that one pathogenic gene for RA in the HLA region is localized in the DRB1 gene, as expected.

a second susceptibility gene of RA was suggested to be present in the HLA class III region, narrowed to 70 kb, that is just telomeric of the TNF gene cluster (TNFA and LTA) and that is located between the microsatellites TNFa and C1-2-A.

findings.statement: Ota et al. (2001) noted that four expressed genes had so far been identified in the critical 70-kb segment: NFKBIL1, ATP6G, BAT1 and MICB, all candidate RA susceptibility genes. The authors stated that their results excluded TNFA (TNF-alpha), previously suggested as a strong candidate for RA in the class III region.
quotes: In this critical segment, four expressed genes have been thus far identified, NFKBIL1 (IkappaBL), ATP6G, BAT1, and MICB, all of which are candidate genes for determining susceptibility to RA.
These results exclude the possibility of involvement of the TNFA genes (TNF-alpha) in the development of RA

relevance_reason: Association study showing a locus in the telomeric HLA region (MIB microsatellite) confers predisposition to RA independently of HLA class II.

findings.statement: Zanelli et al. (2001) analyzed allele distributions of 6 microsatellites in the HLA region (D6S1014, D6S273, TNFalpha, MIB, C1-2-5, and C1-3-2) in 132 RA patients and 254 controls, defining 19 microsatellite clusters corresponding to ancestral haplotypes. The MIB*350 allele, part of a cluster often associated with DQB1*0201-DRB1*0301, was found to be an RA-predisposing factor independent of DRB1*0301 and of the RA-predisposing haplotypes DQB1*03-DRB1*04 and DQB1*0501-DRB1*01. The authors concluded that the telomeric part of the HLA region contains a locus conferring predisposition to RA independently of HLA class II.
quotes: we have looked at the allele distributions of six microsatellites, D6S1014, D6S2673, TNFalpha, MIB, C1-2-5, and C1-3-2 among 132 RA patients and 254 controls
the allele MIB*350 was found to be a RA-predisposing factor, independent of DRB1*0301 and RA-predisposing haplotypes DQB1*03-DRB1*04 and DQB1*0501-DRB1*01
We conclude that the telomeric part of the HLA region contains a locus conferring predisposition to RA independently of HLA class II.

relevance_reason: Expression study of the IL-4 STAT pathway (STAT6) and JAK1 in rheumatoid synovium. It adds pathogenesis context but reports no variants.

findings.statement: Müller-Ladner et al. (2000) used in situ hybridization and immunohistochemistry to study IL-4 STAT and its related kinase Jak-1 in frozen synovial sections from patients with short-term (less than 1 year) and long-term (more than 2 years) rheumatoid arthritis. IL-4 STAT mRNA was found in synovium at both disease stages, most intensely in follicular inflammatory infiltrates, and both fibroblasts and macrophages of the synovial lining expressed it. Synoviocytes expressed IL-4 STAT and Jak-1 protein, IL-4 stimulation up-regulated them, and phosphorylation of IL-4 STAT showed that it was activated. The authors concluded that IL-4 STAT-dependent pathways operate in early and late RA and presumably contribute to inhibitory immune mechanisms in the synovium.
quotes: IL-4 STAT mRNA could be detected in synovium of patients with short-term and long-term RA. The most intensive expression of IL-4 STAT mRNA could be seen in follicular inflammatory infiltrates.
IL-4 STAT and Jak-1 protein was expressed by synoviocytes, and up-regulation could be induced after stimulation with IL-4. Activation of IL-4 STAT was reflected by phosphorylation of IL-4 STAT.
IL-4 STAT-dependent pathways operate in early and late stages of the disease and presumably contribute to inhibitory immune mechanisms in RA synovium

relevance_reason: Reports linkage evidence for the IL-1 gene cluster on 2q13 to rheumatoid arthritis, particularly erosive disease; a susceptibility locus study.

findings.statement: Cox et al. (1999) used the combined sib-TDT and TDT, together with parametric and nonparametric linkage methods, to study the interleukin-1 (IL-1) gene cluster on chromosome 2q13 in RA families. Several tightly linked IL-1 cluster markers gave suggestive evidence for linkage in the combined TDT in families where affected sibs did not share 2 HLA-DRB1 alleles identical by descent, and the evidence was significant in patients with severe, erosive disease. Nonparametric linkage analysis showed no evidence of linkage, but parametric analysis gave weak evidence when marker-trait disequilibrium was included. The authors concluded that the data provided preliminary evidence for linkage of IL-1 cluster genes to RA and suggested a possible role for this region in severe erosive disease.
quotes: Several tightly linked IL-1 cluster markers yielded suggestive evidence for linkage in the combined TDT in those families in which affected siblings did not share two HLA-DRB1 alleles identical by descent.
The evidence was significant in those with severe disease, as assessed by the presence of bone erosions.
The data provide preliminary evidence for linkage of genes of the IL-1 cluster to RA and suggest a possible role for this region in severe erosive disease.

relevance_reason: Rat model (pristane-induced arthritis) linkage study identifying QTLs controlling onset, severity and chronicity of arthritis mimicking RA; animal model evidence for RA entry.

findings.statement: Vingsbo-Lundberg et al. (1998) studied pristane-induced arthritis (PIA) in rats, a model of RA in which a single subcutaneous injection of the non-immunogenic oil pristane into susceptible DA rats induces arthritis restricted to peripheral joints with a chronic relapsing course. They crossed susceptible DA rats with resistant E3 rats; F1 rats developed chronic PIA, indicating dominant genes, but with delayed onset and reduced severity, suggesting recessive and/or additive genes. As in RA, joint involvement was predominantly symmetric, and females were more susceptible than males.
quotes: Pristane is a non-immunogenic synthetic oil that, after a single subcutaneous injection into DA rats, induces arthritis restricted to peripheral joints with a chronic relapsing disease course.

F1 rats developed chronic PIA, indicating dominant genes, but with delayed onset (P<0.0001) and reduced severity ( P<0.0001) compared with the DA parental rats, suggesting incomplete penetrance due to the presence of recessive and/or additive genes.
As in RA, the distribution of affected joints was predominantly symmetric (85% of the affected joints were symmetric at day 35).

findings.statement: Vingsbo-Lundberg et al. (1998) performed a genome screen of 153 (E3xDA) F2 rats with 330 informative microsatellites and found that different arthritis phenotypes were associated with different loci: Pia3 on chromosome 6 and Pia2 on chromosome 4 (significant only in females) controlled arthritis onset; Pia4 on chromosome 12 controlled severity and joint erosion, with linkage also to serum cartilage oligomeric matrix protein (COMP) levels; and Pia5 (chromosome 4, in males) and Pia6 (chromosome 14) controlled chronicity. Loci controlling onset did not influence progression, and chronicity loci were not associated with onset or severity.
quotes: All 153 (E3×DA) F2 rats were subjected to a near-complete genome screen using a set of 330 informative microsatellites.

Loci on chromosomes 4 and 6 (Pia2 and Pia3) influence arthritis onset, whereas a locus on chromosome 12 (Pia4) is associated with severity and joint erosion. We found that chronicity is associated with a different set of loci, one on chromosome 4 and the other on chromosome 14 (Pia5, Pia6).
Loci linked to chronicity (Pia5 and Pia6; Fig. 2f,g,h) were not associated with onset or severity of arthritis (Fig. 4).

findings.statement: Vingsbo-Lundberg et al. (1998) noted that the chronicity locus Pia5 lies near the previously described Cia3 collagen-induced arthritis locus and the Lyp/Iddm1 locus associated with lymphopenia, diabetes, and thyroiditis in the BB rat, which they suggested may indicate a common susceptibility gene for several autoimmune diseases.
quotes: One of the loci controlling chronicity, Pia5, is located in the vicinity of the previously described Cia3 locus, which controls collagen-induced arthritis, and the Lyp/Iddm1 locus, which is associated with lymphopenia, diabetes and thyroiditis in the BB rat, (Fig. 3).
This may indicate the presence of a common susceptibility gene for several autoimmune diseases.

relevance_reason: Genome-wide linkage scan in RA sib pairs that identified HLA plus 14 candidate regions, and replicated a putative susceptibility locus at 3q13.

findings.statement: Cornélis et al. (1998) carried out a genome scan in 114 European Caucasian RA sib pairs from 97 nuclear families. Linkage was significant only for HLA (P < 2.5 x 10(-5)). It was nominal (P < 0.05) for 19 markers in 14 other regions, 4 of which possibly overlap with loci implicated in IDDM (IDDM6, IDDM9, IDDM13, and DXS998).
quotes: A genome scan was performed with 114 European Caucasian RA sib pairs from 97 nuclear families. Linkage was significant only for HLA (P < 2.5.10(-5)) and nominal for 19 markers in 14 other regions (P < 0.05).
Four of the loci implicated in IDDM potentially overlap with these regions: the putative IDDM6, IDDM9, IDDM13, and DXS998 loci.

findings.statement: Cornélis et al. (1998) examined the 18q22-q23 candidate region (D18S68-D18S61-D18S469) and the 3q13 candidate region (D3S1267) in a further 194 RA sib pairs from 164 nuclear families. Only the chromosome 3 region showed significantly extended support for linkage (P = 0.002). Across all 261 families the evidence for linkage was P = 0.001, and the authors suggested that this putative RA locus interacts with HLA. They estimated that the locus could account for 16% of the genetic component of RA and proposed the genes encoding CD80 and CD86 as candidates.
quotes: were studied in 194 additional RA sib pairs from 164 nuclear families. Support for linkage to chromosome 3 only was extended significantly (P = 0.002).

The analysis of all 261 families provided a linkage evidence of P = 0. 001 and suggested an interaction between this putative RA locus and HLA. This locus could account for 16% of the genetic component of RA.
Candidate genes include those coding for CD80 and CD86, molecules involved in antigen-specific T cell recognition.

findings.statement: Cornélis et al. (1998) noted that familial aggregation (lambda-s = 5), twin studies, and segregation analysis suggest a genetic component to RA. HLA, the only known susceptibility locus, had been estimated to account for one-third of this component.
quotes: Its genetic component has been suggested by familial aggregation (lambdas = 5), twin studies, and segregation analysis. HLA, which is the only susceptibility locus known, has been estimated to account for one-third of this component.

relevance_reason: Transgenic mouse model showing that HLA-DQ polymorphism (DQ8 vs DQ6) affects how often collagen-induced arthritis occurs and how severe it is; supports a role for HLA-DQ in RA susceptibility.

findings.statement: Bradley et al. (1997) produced mice transgenic for HLA-DQ6, an allele associated with a nonsusceptible haplotype, and found that they were resistant to collagen-induced arthritis (CIA). The authors had previously shown that mice transgenic for HLA-DQ8, an RA-associated allele, developed severe arthritis after immunization with type II collagen.
quotes: we generated mice transgenic for HLA-DQ6, an allele associated with a nonsusceptible haplotype. The DQ6 mice were found to be resistant to collagen-induced arthritis.
We have previously demonstrated that mice transgenic for HLA-DQ8, a DQ allele associated with susceptibility to RA, develop severe arthritis after type II collagen immunization.

findings.statement: Bradley et al. (1997) found that double-transgenic mice expressing both HLA-DQ6 and HLA-DQ8 developed moderate collagen-induced arthritis, whereas DQ8 transgenic mice developed severe arthritis. The authors compared this to RA patients who carry both susceptible and nonsusceptible HLA haplotypes and concluded that the results support a role for HLA-DQ polymorphism in human RA.
quotes: The double-transgenic mice developed moderate CIA when immunized with CII when compared with the severe arthritis observed in DQ8 transgenic mice, much like RA patients bearing both susceptible and nonsusceptible HLA haplotypes.
These studies support a role for HLA-DQ polymorphism in human RA.

relevance_reason: The paper reports a rat animal model of rheumatoid arthritis (pristane-induced arthritis) with evidence that both MHC and non-MHC genes influence susceptibility and chronicity; relevant as animal model evidence in a rheumatoid arthritis entry.

findings.statement: Vingsbo et al. (1996) presented pristane-induced arthritis in rats as a novel animal model for rheumatoid arthritis; 2 weeks after a single intradermal injection of 150 microliters of the synthetic adjuvant oil pristane, rats developed severe and chronic arthritis in which the inflammation was restricted to the joints and involved pannus formation, MHC class II expression, and T-lymphocyte infiltration.
quotes: We present a novel animal model for rheumatoid arthritis induced with a well defined synthetic adjuvant oil, pristane.

Two weeks after a single intradermal injection of 150 microliters of pristane, the rats developed severe and chronic arthritis. The inflammation was restricted to the joints and involved pannus formation, major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class II expression, and T lymphocyte infiltration.

findings.statement: Vingsbo et al. (1996) found that both the initial development and the chronic stage of pristane-induced arthritis in rats were ameliorated by treatment with antibodies to the alpha-beta T-cell receptor, showing that the disease is T cell dependent.
quotes: The initial development as well as the chronic stage of pristane-induced arthritis was ameliorated by treatment with antibodies to the alpha beta-T-cell receptor showing that the disease is T cell dependent.

findings.statement: In the rat pristane-induced arthritis model, Vingsbo et al. (1996) observed increased serum levels of interleukin after pristane injection but not during the chronic stage of arthritis, and joint erosions were accompanied by elevated serum levels of cartilage oligomeric matrix protein.
quotes: Increased levels of interleukin in serum was seen after pristane injection but not during the chronic stage of arthritis. Joint erosions were accompanied by elevated serum levels of cartilage oligomeric matrix protein.

phenotypes.text: elevated serum cartilage oligomeric matrix protein

findings.statement: Comparing MHC congenic LEW rat strains, Vingsbo et al. (1996) showed that the severity and chronicity of pristane-induced arthritis varied among the different MHC haplotypes, with rats of the RT1f haplotype showing significantly higher susceptibility; a strong influence of non-MHC genes was also suggested by the variability of arthritis susceptibility among different strains sharing the same MHC haplotype, the most susceptible background being DA and the least susceptible E3.
quotes: Comparison of MHC congenic LEW strains showed that the severity and chronicity of arthritis varied among the different MHC haplotypes. Rats with RT1f haplotype showed a significantly higher susceptibility to pristane-induced arthritis.

A strong influence of non-MHC genes was also suggested by the variability of arthritis susceptibility among different strains with the same MHC haplotype; the most susceptible background was the DA and the least susceptible was the E3.
findings.population: rat (MHC congenic LEW, DA, E3 strains)

findings.statement: Vingsbo et al. (1996) concluded that arthritis induced with a well defined nonimmunogenic adjuvant, with a disease course closely resembling that of rheumatoid arthritis, makes a suitable animal model for future studies of the pathology and genetics of rheumatoid arthritis.
quotes: Arthritis induced with a well defined nonimmunogenic adjuvant, with a disease course that closely resembles that of rheumatoid arthritis, makes a suitable animal model for future studies of the pathology and genetics of rheumatoid arthritis.

relevance_reason: Twin study of TCRBJ gene usage in RA-discordant monozygotic twins; shows genetic control of TCR repertoire not altered by RA inflammation. Adds pathogenesis context.

findings.statement: Nanki et al. (1996) used a PCR-ELISA method to study T cell receptor BJ gene expression in peripheral T lymphocytes from 12 pairs of monozygotic twins, including 6 pairs discordant for rheumatoid arthritis, and 5 normal individuals, focusing on the TCRBV5, 13, and 17 families reported to be increased in RA. BJ gene repertoires of monozygotic twins were more similar than those of unrelated individuals, and RA inflammation did not induce specific changes in the genetically determined pattern of BJ expression. The authors concluded that the frequency of expression of particular TCRBV-TCRBJ recombinants is genetically controlled and maintained despite chronic inflammatory disease.
quotes: compared peripheral T lymphocytes from 12 pairs of monozygotic twins, including 6 rheumatoid arthritis (RA) discordant pairs, and 5 normals

(c) the BJ gene repertoires of monozygotic twins are more similar than those of unrelated individuals; and (d) the inflammation of RA does not induce specific changes in the genetically determined pattern of BJ expression

These results indicate that the frequency of expression particular TCRBV-TCRBJ recombinants in human lymphocytes is controlled genetically, and is maintained despite the presence of a chronic inflammatory disease.

relevance_reason: Only the title is available; it is a general review of the genetics of autoimmune disease. It may give context for rheumatoid arthritis, but the title has no findings specific to RA.

findings.statement: Vyse and Todd (1996) reviewed the genetic analysis of autoimmune disease.
quotes: Genetic analysis of autoimmune disease.

relevance_reason: Only the title ("Rheumatoid arthritis.") was supplied. This is a short review in Cell on rheumatoid arthritis. The text contains no patients, variants or data that could support a quoted finding.
Provides a transgenic mouse model implicating HLA-DQ8 in susceptibility to arthritis, relevant as animal-model evidence for the rheumatoid arthritis entry.

findings.statement: Nabozny et al. (1996) generated transgenic mice expressing the HLA-DQA1*0301 and DQB1*0302 genes from a rheumatoid arthritis-predisposing haplotype (DQ8/DR4Dw4) on a mouse class II-deficient H-2Ab0 background, and found that the HLA-DQ8+,H-2Ab0 mice expressed the DQ8 molecule well with no detectable surface expression of endogenous murine class II molecules and selected CD4+ T cells with a normal V beta T cell receptor repertoire.
quotes: To examine the role of HLA-DQ molecules in arthritis, we generated transgenic mice expressing the DQA1*0301 and DQB1*0302 genes from an RA predisposing haplotype (DQ8/DR4Dw4).

The HLA-DQ8+,H-2Ab0 mice displayed good expression of the DQ8 molecule, while no surface expression of endogenous murine class II molecules could be detected. The DQ8 molecule also induced the selection of CD4+ T cells expressing a normal repertoire of V beta T cell receptors.

findings.statement: Nabozny et al. (1996) reported that immunization of HLA-DQ8+,H-2Ab0 transgenic mice with bovine type II collagen induced a strong antibody response cross-reactive with homologous mouse type II collagen and in vitro proliferative responses that were blocked by antibodies specific for HLA-DQ and mouse CD4, and that a severe polyarthritis developed in a majority of the mice, indistinguishable from the disease in arthritis-susceptible B10.T(6R) (H-2Aq) controls, whereas HLA-DQ8-negative,H-2Ab0 full sibs generated no collagen antibody and were completely resistant to arthritis.
quotes: Immunization of HLA-DQ8+,H-2Ab0 mice with bovine type II collagen (CII) induced a strong antibody response that was cross-reactive to homologous mouse CII.

Finally, a severe polyarthritis developed in a majority of HLA-DQ8+,H-2Ab0 mice, which was indistinguishable from the disease observed in arthritis susceptible B10.T(6R) (H-2Aq) controls. In contrast, HLA-DQ8-,H-2Ab0 fullsibs did not generate CII antibody and were completely resistant to arthritis.

findings.statement: Nabozny et al. (1996) concluded that their results strongly suggested that HLA-DQ8 molecules contribute to genetic susceptibility to arthritis and established a novel animal model for the study of human arthritis.
quotes: Therefore, these results strongly suggest that HLA-DQ8 molecules contribute to genetic susceptibility to arthritis and also establish a novel animal model for the study of human arthritis.

findings.statement: Nabozny et al. (1996) noted that genetic studies had indicated that susceptibility to rheumatoid arthritis (RA) maps to the HLA-DR locus of the major histocompatibility complex, and that strong linkage disequilibrium between certain HLA-DQ genes and RA-associated HLA-DR genes suggested that HLA-DQ molecules may also play a role in RA susceptibility.
quotes: Genetic studies have indicated that susceptibility to rheumatoid arthritis (RA) maps to the HLA-DR locus of the major histocompatibility complex. Strong linkage disequilibrium between certain HLA-DQ genes and HLA-DR genes associated with RA, however, suggests that HLA-DQ molecules may also play a role in RA susceptibility.

relevance_reason: Segregation/likelihood analysis of multiplex RA pedigrees characterizing an HLA-linked susceptibility locus (inheritance model, penetrance, allele frequency).

findings.statement: Hasstedt et al. (1994) studied 28 pedigrees ascertained through pairs of first-degree relatives with rheumatoid arthritis, in which RA was confirmed in 77 members and absence of disease verified in 261 members, all serologically typed for HLA. Likelihood analysis assuming tight linkage to HLA supported an HLA-linked RA susceptibility locus with a susceptibility allele frequency of 2.16% and lifetime penetrance of 41% in male and 48% in female homozygotes; inheritance was recessive in males and nearly recessive in females.
quotes: Twenty-eight pedigrees were ascertained through pairs of first-degree relatives diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis (RA). RA was confirmed in 77 pedigree members including probands; the absence of disease was verified in an additional 261 pedigree members.

The analysis supported the existence of an HLA-linked RA susceptibility locus, estimated the susceptibility allele frequency as 2.16%, and estimated the lifetime penetrance as 41% in male homozygotes and as 48% in female homozygotes.
Inheritance was recessive in males and was nearly recessive in females.

findings.statement: Hasstedt et al. (1994) estimated that the HLA-linked RA susceptibility locus accounts for approximately one-half of familial RA but only about one-fifth of RA in the population, suggesting that other genes may account for the remaining familial RA and that a large portion of cases may occur sporadically. The analysis attributed 78% of the variance within genotypes to genetic or environmental effects shared by siblings.
quotes: The inferred HLA-linked RA susceptibility locus accounts for approximately one-half of familial RA, although it accounts for only approximately one-fifth of the RA in the population.
Although other genes may account for the remaining familial RA, a large portion of RA cases may occur sporadically.
the analysis attributed 78% of the variance within genotypes to genetic or environmental effects shared by siblings

relevance_reason: Segregation analysis and family study of RA showing a recessive major gene model and heterogeneity of risk by proband gender; relevant to inheritance and heterogeneity sections.

findings.statement: Lynn et al. (1995) did family studies and segregation analyses of rheumatoid arthritis based on consecutive patients ascertained without regard to family history, including first-degree relatives from 135 simplex and 30 multiplex families. A highly penetrant recessive major gene with a mutant allele frequency of 0.005 was identified as the most parsimonious genetic risk factor.
quotes: First-degree relatives from 135 simplex and 30 multiplex families were included in the analyses.
A highly penetrant recessive major gene, with a mutant allele frequency of .005, was identified as the most parsimonious genetic risk factor.

findings.statement: Lynn et al. (1995) found significant heterogeneity in RA risk by proband gender but not by proband age at onset. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed that both proband gender and age at onset were risk factors, with proband gender the more important determinant; relatives of male probands had the greatest cumulative risk. Log-linear modeling found proband gender, familiality (multiplex or simplex), and their interaction adequate to define risk in families, and the authors concluded that the pattern of risk and its inheritance is heterogeneous.
quotes: Significant evidence for heterogeneity in risk for RA was observed for proband gender but not for proband age at onset.
proband gender appears to be the more important determinant of risk, with relatives of male probands having the greatest cumulative risk for RA.
The pattern of risk for RA among susceptible individuals and its inheritance is thus heterogeneous.

findings.statement: Lynn et al. (1995) suggested that families with an excess of affected males with young age at onset may be the most informative for identifying the putative recessive gene and its modifiers.
quotes: For future genetic analyses, families with an excess of affected males having a young age at onset may be the most informative in identifying the putative recessive gene and its modifiers.

relevance_reason: Only the title is available. It shows that the paper proposes the 'shared epitope hypothesis' as a framework for the molecular genetics of rheumatoid arthritis susceptibility, which is a central concept for this entry.

findings.statement: Gregersen et al. (1987) proposed the shared epitope hypothesis as an approach to understanding the molecular genetics of susceptibility to rheumatoid arthritis.
quotes: The shared epitope hypothesis. An approach to understanding the molecular genetics of susceptibility to rheumatoid arthritis.

relevance_reason: Describes an inherited deficiency of monocyte non-specific esterase that runs in families, seen in 4 patients with rheumatoid arthritis. It is an associated biochemical finding with no gene identified.

findings.statement: Bell et al. (1992) described deficiency of the monocyte ectoenzyme non-specific esterase in 4 patients with rheumatoid arthritis. The deficiency followed a heredofamilial pattern. They found no association of the deficiency with HLA status or with rheumatoid factor seropositivity.
quotes: Deficiency of the monocyte ectoenzyme non-specific esterase is described in a heredofamilial pattern in four patients with rheumatoid arthritis.
No association with HLA status or rheumatoid factor seropositivity was found.

relevance_reason: Genotype-phenotype study of HLA-DRB1 allele combinations and extraarticular manifestations in RA patients.

findings.statement: Weyand et al. (1992) stratified 81 patients with seropositive rheumatoid arthritis by disease manifestations and typed HLA-DRB1 alleles by PCR and oligonucleotide hybridization, confirming homozygosity by locus-specific cDNA amplification and sequencing. They found that rheumatoid nodules were highly associated with heterozygosity for 2 disease-associated HLA-DRB1 alleles, whereas homozygosity for HLA-DRB1*0401 was characteristic of RA patients with major organ involvement.
quotes: We have stratified 81 patients according to their patterns of disease manifestations and identified the HLA-DRB1 alleles by polymerase chain reaction amplification and subsequent oligonucleotide hybridization.
Rheumatoid nodules were highly associated with a heterozygosity for two disease associated HLA-DRB1 alleles.
Homozygosity for the HLA-DRB1*0401 allele was a characteristic finding for RA patients with major organ involvement.

findings.statement: Weyand et al. (1992) suggested that the disease-associated sequence motif in the third hypervariable region of HLA-DRB1 plays a role in determining RA severity, and that the codominant function of HLA-DRB1 alleles implies that HLA-DR function in thymic selection might be important in RA pathogenesis.
quotes: Our data suggest a role of the disease-associated sequence motif in determining severity of the disease.
The finding of a codominant function of HLA-DRB1 alleles suggests that the biological function of HLA-DR molecules in thymic selection might be important in the pathogenesis of RA.

relevance_reason: HLA-D association study contrasting juvenile and adult RA; shows that HLA-DW4, the antigen associated with adult RA, is not increased in juvenile RA.

findings.statement: Stastny and Fink (1979) performed HLA-D typing in 126 patients with juvenile rheumatoid arthritis. HLA-DW4, the antigen associated with adult rheumatoid arthritis in earlier studies, was significantly less frequent in children with arthritis than in normal controls (P less than 0.04). In contrast, HLA-DW7 (P less than 0.03) and HLA-DW8 (P less than 0.01) were increased in the children. The authors concluded that adult rheumatoid arthritis and arthritis of childhood differ fundamentally.
quotes: HLA-D typing was performed in 126 patients with juvenile rheumatoid arthritis. HLA-DW4, the antigen found in previous studies to characterize adult rheumatoid arthritis, had a significantly lower frequency in children with arthritis than in normal controls (P less than 0.04).
By contrast, in children the antigens HLA-DW7 (P less than 0.03) and HLA-DW8 (P less than 0.01) were increased compared to controls.
These results provide evidence of fundamental differences between adult rheumatoid arthritis and arthritis of childhood.

findings.statement: Stastny and Fink (1979) found that TMo, an HLA-D antigen detected with homozygous typing cells from a child with juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, was related to the cross-reactive specificities HLA-DW7 and DW11. TMo was present in 46% of patients with persistent pauciarticular arthritis of childhood, compared with 1% of normal controls, giving a relative risk of 67.7 (P less than 0.0001). The authors suggested that childhood arthritis includes a clinically distinguishable group characterized by TMo.
quotes: The antigen TMo, detected with homozygous typing cells from a child with juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, was found to be related to the cross-reactive specificities HLA-DW7 and DW11.

46% of the patients with persistent pauciarticular arthritis of childhood typed for the antigen TMo, compared to only 1% of normal controls. Thus the relative risk for persistent pauciarticular arthritis in relation to the presence of TMo was 67.7 (P less than 0.0001).
